title: GWR delay repay and refund portal site…
content: GWR delay repay and refund portal site has to be the most cumbersome, frustrating and unuser friendly online form ever produced. Deliberately set out in 8 steps to annoy the user. just spent best part of 40 mins trying to claim a refund for one journey. It asks you all these fiddly details which they can retrieve from your booking number, but they want you to manually enter it in, it then by default says it wants an alternative payment method to pay the refund on, well I don't want to provide an additional account or card details for a refund, I just want the refund made to my original payment card. If you happen to enter card details for a Mastercard it then tells you that they are having problems with Mastercard payments and to provide a bank account number or a Visa card number. On top of that (which really was the final straw) when you upload your E-ticket it RESETS EVERYTHING and takes you to the first page. Absolutely DIABOLICAL!! They do this so you give up processing a refund for a cancelled service. I would rather spend more time writing up an honest review here than using their refund portal

content: Why aren't you providing the service that you promised?! I'm sick to death of the incompetence of this so called company. Trains delayed, always overcrowded. title: I rarely write reviews
content: I rarely write reviews, but the service I received from Adrian at Great Western Railway today (journey from Swindon to Bristol) was so extraordinary, it compelled me to share. From the moment I approached him, he radiated genuine warmth and a willingness to help. I was facing some very serious personal challenges and he went above and beyond to resolve it.Not only did he efficiently solve my problem, but he did so with a level of kindness and empathy that truly brightened my day. He reminded me of the power of human connection.It wasn't just about fixing a problem; it was about the way he made me feel – valued, understood, and genuinely cared for. If I could give more than 5 stars, I absolutely would. This individual deserves not just recognition, but a standing ovation. Thank you, Adrian, for turning a potentially stressful situation into a truly positive experience. You are a credit to Great Western Railway, and I hope your exceptional service is celebrated because it wasn’t only exceptional customer service but also exceptional customer care and this combination is rare. May God bless you plenty!!

Thing's go wrong, we all accept that, but not offering proper compensation is a disgrace and reflection of trains in the UK

title: Don’t claim a refund if your train is delayed …
content: Recently travelled from Exeter to Canterbury West. The Exeter to Paddington GWR train was cancelled at Taunton because of a police incident that closed the line. The train was sent back to Exeter where I waited for the next Paddington train to run once the line was reopened. I’d anticipated getting back to Canterbury at 20.25, but arrived after 22.30. The lovely staff on the GWR train were helpful and told us we’d all get a refund - claiming was easy. So I claimed, only to have my claim rejected because my original, cancelled train was not on their timetable ie. it didn’t exist. As part of my claim I uploaded photos of my tickets clearly showing the time of the train and my seat booking. It was an advance ticket so I could only travel on that specific train. I also have the journey schedule from Trainline clearly showing my journey times. The automated email declining my refund offered me a chance to appeal, but in reality it just asks for the same info again and sets up a new claim. My feeling is that this is a tactic to put people off claiming what they’re entitled to. As I said earlier - train staff were brilliant, but GWR process/treatment of customers is terrible.

title: Appalling Customer Service
content: My partner and I were thoroughly disgusted and disappointed with the way we were treated by this company.  We were informed only slightly before we were due to board our train from London Paddington to Cardiff Central, that it had been cancelled due to a lack of staff.  This message appeared on the notice board.  It also stated that you couldn’t board the next train to Cardiff if you had saver tickets (which we did have as part of our journey package).  We had to catch a later train which led to us missing our connection in Cardiff and being many hours late arriving at our destination.  GWR’s claim website states the following regarding compensation for delayed or cancelled trains:‘How much you get will depend on the type of ticket you have and how late you arrived at your  destination’The maximum claim of a 100 per cent refund definitely applies as it was definitely over 120 minutes as our train NEVER arrived.  And, we were definitely more than 120 minutes late arriving at our destination.  Therefore, we were appalled when GWR decided to amend our claim form, with their own version of how long we were delayed.  When questioned they said that this was because there was another train which we could have taken which would have meant a shorter delay, but our tickets meant we couldn’t take this train – this was clearly explained on the notice board.We then appealed and liaised with GWR for two months trying to resolve this issue.  Each time we contacted them there was a long delay before we received a response.  I finally asked for details of their complaints procedure but never received this information.  I was told that my correspondence had been passed to a manager but despite making it clear that I wish to complain – not merely provide feedback – I have not had a response from a manager.  If anyone from GWR happens to be reading this, please sort out your staffing levels so that you can cope with any eventualities that arise on any given day.  Also, please bear in mind that it was your fault that we were put in the situation that we were in, due to you cancelling our train, the least you could do is pay appropriate compensation – for a cancelled train – in a timely manner and without quibbling – remember, you caused this situation.

title: Impossible Compensation Process for Cancelled Train
content: I had an awful experience with GWR when my train was cancelled in November. I had to buy a second ticket at significant cost, only to be forced to stand in a packed aisle for the entire journey from London to Bristol, despite having originally booked a seat. Given the high cost of train tickets, this was completely unacceptable.The compensation process has been just as frustrating. Despite repeatedly submitting the required train details and ticket receipt, my claim has been rejected multiple times, with vague requests for "more information"—yet no clear guidance on what is actually needed. It feels like they are deliberately making it difficult for passengers to claim refunds.To make matters worse, the complaints form on their website is faulty. I tried submitting my complaint, but it kept failing due to so-called "special characters"—even though I wasn’t using any. This just adds to the feeling that they don’t actually want to hear from customers.I'm out over £100 due to their cancellation and missed an important event as a result. Their lack of accountability, poor customer service, and broken complaints process make it clear that they do not care about their passengers. Extremely disappointing experience.

title: A huge thank you for the GWR staff saving my day
content: This morning it was so wet that I was carrying my umbrella, usually something you leave on a train, but instead I left my handbag on the train at Dawlish as I had a case as well.  I realised as soon as I got in the lift but as I looked in horror my heart sinking, the train pulled out for Teignmouth. Panic followed.  Luckily Jimmy was the station master on platform 1, he got straight on the phone to Teignmouth and my bag was intercepted at Teignmouth Station and popped on the next train back to Dawlish arriving before my Paddington train arrived.  I cannot thank Jimmy and the driver of the train from Teignmouth enough, they saved my day. The staff are so helpful. They deserve a huge pat on the back. My journey to London today was very important to me so a huge thank you and 5 stars from me.

title: Great Western Russian Roulette – A GWR Adventure Every Month
content: Riding GWR is not just about getting from A to B. No, my friends, it’s a thrilling gamble, a journey into the unknown, a test of patience and existential endurance. After two years of commuting this route multiple times a month, I’ve come to accept that "on time" is not a concept GWR recognizes.Let’s talk about today’s masterpiece:Train stops "in the middle of nowhere" (classic move).Train stands still for an hour, teasing passengers with the possibility of movement.Instead of reaching my destination, train casually decides to go back the way it came. Why? Mystery. Swindon magic.I’ve taken this delightful Russian Roulette ride dozens of times, and I can count on one hand the times it was actually on schedule. GWR’s approach to travel isn’t about efficiency, it’s about building character. Can you handle uncertainty? Do you enjoy spontaneous route changes? Are you ready to embrace fate?Refunds? Compensation? Who cares! I don’t want a £5 voucher, I just want to be where I need to be, on time, without feeling like I’m in a Monty Python sketch.But hey, if you love the thrill of unpredictability, if you enjoy turning a simple journey into a logistical adventure, then GWR is the experience you’ve been looking for. 10/10 for drama, 0/10 for reliability.Would I recommend it?If you’re on a schedule – NO.If you enjoy gambling with your arrival time – ABSOLUTELY!Great Western Russian Roulette – every ride is a new surprise!

title: Shoutout to my fav GWR employee
content: Recently travelled on GWR train for the first time to visit Exeter for work. Trip up to Exeter was fine, but the trip back not so much. Ashley, lovely employee that he is, was checking tickets on the train on this fine day. Upon checking mine, Ashley pointed out that I happened to have misread the time on my advanced single ticket and boarded a train one hour before the train listed. Same route, same day, one hour early. I said “oh gosh so sorry” and Ashley explained how I’d still need to get the same connecting train to my final destination. I said yes, that was the plan.  At this point, Ashley advises me that, due to the fact I am on a train one hour earlier than originally planned, I must now pay full price for an entirely new ticket to cover my entire journey. I was somewhat taken aback by this because 1) the “incorrect” train would only apply for part of the journey - why would I pay for a new ticket for the entire journey 2) It’s the same exact route, I’m sitting in a seat marked available, I’m still planning to get the same connecting train, neither of the times would coincide with rush hour or a different route or higher prices. 3) It was made blatantly clear during our conversation that this was a mistake, to be honest what on earth would be the benefit of deliberately booking the train an hour later than when I planned to get it? That would’ve had absolutely no impact on the price when booking and I know this for a fact. I was so in awe of this that I perhaps didn’t push back enough on it. Another passenger did attempt to question it on my behalf, but Ashley was steadfast. We managed to wrangle it down to just paying for the ticket between Exeter and my change over point. I didn’t even have the chance to request that my railcard was applied before a card machine was shoved in my face and I was requested to pay an absolutely insane price of £62.80Again, all because I misread a ticket and got a train ONE HOUR earlier than I was supposed to. Insane and ridiculous policy that Ashley was very very happy to enforce. I would’ve been happy to pay the difference between the cost of my original ticket and an open single, I would even have been begrudgingly willing to pay the fare with my railcard applied. Realistically I should not have had to pay anything at all. If you want me to get off at the next stop and wait one hour for the other train, sure I’d do it. The times at which the trains were would not have had any impact whatsoever on price and I think it was extremely clear - even to other passengers around me who challenged Ashley on my behalf - that this was a mistake. Insane dedication to the company Ashley, hopefully they’ll promote you for all the profit you bring in from scamming customers out of money because they’re too polite to fight you on it.

If GWR was an injured racehorse if would have been put out of its misery long ago.To all the overpaid executives laughing into their morning coffee at the one star reviews posted on this forum, I offer this advice. Your concept of 'Cancellation without Explanation' works a treat. No need to offer any apology or reason whatsoever when trains get cancelled. Ditto any delay. But wait, why even bother trying to stick to a timetable? Just run a train at random times throughout the day and collect anyone waiting patiently at a station. Remember, happy customers, happy stakeholders. You can thank me later.

title: Overpriced Poor Service
content: I have used GWR many times over my lifetime and they’ve always been 50/50 but only since Sep 2024 started using multiple times a week for commuting between Chippenham and London. My early morning trains have thus far been OK, which accounts for the two stars, but in general the evening and weekend trains have been awful. By default, the Bristol or Weston Super Mare trains are always the very last to be given a platform at Paddington, resulting in a mad scrummage as commuters and tourists alike scramble to the train with only a few minutes to go. Often the carriage letter isn't marked on the trains for a couple of minutes after gates open resulting in everyone rushing back and forth up the platform trying to figure where their reservations are in a mad panic. On two occasions only half the train arrived resulting in standing the full 1h 10 journey like sardines in a crushed tin box. On a few occasions there have been no reservations due to other issues (amending stops or other passengers moved trains due to cancellations) which again has caused people to stand (including the elderly and mothers with young children). Furthermore, I had cancellations and chaos all day Sunday 10 November as half the train drivers didn't show up to work (heard it directly from two GWR ticket inspectors at Paddington) and on Tuesday 12 November had another day on tenterhooks as once again ’disruption’ on the lines. I have paid out a lot of additional money in cabs and other travel as a result. What more, Wifi has never worked. No exaggeration, not once on any of my trains. Finally to boot, the trains are very expensive. I have paid between £66 and £75 on most occasions (return) and have a couple at £55. Really poor. I appreciate the lazy and overpaid train drivers in this country and their unions have us all over a barrel / to ransom but GWR need to get this sorted or drastically lower the price of fares. I’m not looking for some lame apology here, just stating it as experienced across sixteen trips since October. Finally, contradictory to the overall company mantra, it’s worth highlighting the ticket inspectors and catering cart staff are great and I can’t fault them on 99% of travel so applaud their conscientiousness.

title: Bring on public ownership! GWR couldnt run to the shops let alone a railway
content: Booked an exciting trip to Newquay from London. Arrived at Paddington to find out the train has been completely cancelled, and instead a service is running from Reading (ie not Paddington, not even London). They (very kindly assisted and) advised me to hop on the train on platform 8 to reading and catch it from there. Sure, fine by me.I arrive at the platform. The visibly stressed and clearly unsupported train manager, who as a result is incredibly kurt and borderline aggressive, doesn't let me board because i require a bike space reservation, which of course i dont have for this random train to Reading. So he refuses to let me board the train despite the fact the bike spaces were empty two minutes before departure and I was only going a one stop. Ended up getting a coach from National Express instead who were incredibly friendly and helpful.Its obviously not the train managers fault, but the lack of staff and support deployed by GWR amid cancellations. GWR's reckless operation of the railway continues to prioritising profits and shareholders and greed, over offering an effective or safe service to the public or even a reasonable place to work.

title: Hard painful seats for a long journey
content: We took the train to London from Cardiff and back on Wed 16th October as a change from driving.  It was expensive but we thought we'd give it a try and bought a Two Together railcard to bring the fare down a bit.  The outward journey was fine albeit we arrived about 10 mins late but the return journey was fraught with problems at Bristol Parkway and so we  were 45 mins late on our return.  I have applied for a refund, we'll see how that goes..........However my main complaint is about the train itself.  Like an earlier reviewer on this site I have never, ever sat on such uncomfortable seats on any form of public transport either here or in other countries.  They are essentially hard moulded plastic with a bit of  material stuck over them.  They must have been designed by a robot as they certainly can't have been designed and tested by a human being who has any feeling in their backside.  I am actually a female with  more than adequate "padding" on my backside but these seats caused agony.  There is a rounded plastic part across the middle of the seat which just digs into  you.  I am writing this the day after my trip and by backside and thighs are still aching from the seating. Laughingly, the seats we sat on for our return had an illustration to show that they were designated for pregnant women and the elderly.  Neither of these groups I'm sure would be able to tolerate these seats for any length of time.  Borrowing from another review - "Let the train cause the pain" would be a suitable slogan for these trains they are awful.  I would use the service again however I would definitely come armed with an inflatable pillow to make the journey bearable.  Come on GWR - spend some money on refurbishing your seats !!

title: Two hour delay and took back their refund
content: In May 2024 I took the GWR. The train was over two hours delayed. As per the GWR policy, I was entitled to a full refund. I applied for the refund and received the cheque. A few months later, GWR cancelled the cheque and the money was withdrawn from my account with additional fees. I contacted GWR right away to find out the reason for this and their reply was “some international banks do not accept our cheques.” Clearly mine did as it was deposited and I had no issues. It has now been almost six weeks and GWR has not returned the money but instead just replies to me that they are still investigating. I have sent them proof from my bank of the amount that was withdrawn, but this does not seem to be enough. To a large corporation like GWR this may not seem like much money but to me, $518.00 CAD unexpectedly withdrawn from my account has been very hard. I am very disappointed in the way that GWR has handled the situation.

title: ‘Quiet Carriage’ I don’t think you understand what that word means
content: Constant delays and uncomfortable seats are standard on these trains, but my biggest issue is the so called ‘quiet’ carriage. I’m Autistic so a quiet carriage would really help me, I always book it and it is never quiet. The staff do nothing to enforce it. It makes an already uncomfortable experience almost unbearable. I travel between Cardiff and London regularly and it is always the same. I contacted their social media on one occasion and was told to speak to the staff on board, well there was nobody to be seen, but also I shouldn’t have to do this. I’m not confident to confront every single person myself.  I tried to complain directly on their website but it would not allow me to submit because apparently they don’t manage the stations??? I don’t know how they are getting away with not accepting complaints this way. My complaint has nothing to do with the station!!! I’m so fed up of being disappointed by this lack of service. We should know better by now about Autistic people and others with similar traits and how we are impacted by this type of thing. The quiet carriage is basically false advertising. GWR you need to do better.

title: I travelled to London from Cardiff on…
content: I travelled to London from Cardiff on Wednesday, 9th October, and returned on the 14th. In both cases since the train service was between Paddington and Cardiff only and no further west what appears to be fairly new trains were used. And they are awful! The seats are hard and very uncomfortable. The new slogan should be let the train take the strain and give you pain! And no trolley service in either direction. I believe the lack of trolley service may be due to a design fault. The doors between carriages near the toilets with baby changing facilities are too close to the large structure of the toilets leaving no room for a trolley to pass. I've used train travel between Cardiff and London for decades going from a buffet car with an array of choice to a trolley service you might see twice during a journey to an intermittent trolley service to no trolley at all. Whoever signed off the design and equipment on these trains must be in a very senior position and so paid an awful lot of money. They should be sacked as incompetent and not up to the job. Train travel, for comfort and facilities, has hit a new low.

title: If you like standing and huge delays…

I got the whole of my fare back though the delay repay of £140.60. Just make sure you've planned your journey at the other end well in advance as you won't get to your destination on time

title: GWR employee told me to f off
content: I've made the decision never to get a GWR train again tonight and to state from the outset I wasn't even that badly delayed!I arrived at Paddington with a couple of minutes to spare to catch the last train to Hanborough (not blaming anyone for that bit of course!) And was amazed to see even though I was literally standing at Platform 8 which is where my train was departing from, there was no information on the respective message boards. Good start.To compound matters further, when I panickedly asked a GWR employee standing doing nothing  (other than chatting to another on the platform) if this was my train, I was not only not told which train it was, but was, and I quote here, told to "f*** off" in response to my pretty ordinary enquiry. Given there was literally seconds before my departure time, it was a fairly abrupt question I'll admit, but to be responded to in such a way is an absolute disgrace. And then to sum it all up, when I actually got on the train (asking a fellow passenger if it was in fact my train given there was no evidence of that so far) the first thing I heard was an announcement that there wasn't in fact a crew ready to operate the train!I mean really you have to laugh at this point, but it shouldn't be a laughing matter. GWR charges extortionate prices for their services (I'm not qualified to comment on why) but given that frankly extortionate demand, the very least they could do is employ competent, polite people. I know this won't come to anything other than a fake apology from a distant GWR employee who has no relation whatsoever to the initial incident, but if I don't say anything, nothing happens at all. GWR, whether you want to or not, you represent a nation, and if anyone judges the UK by your services, then that is a truly shocking indictment.

Anyone who works for FGW is a fraud and every time they cash their paychecks they are robbing the people who have to pay such high fees for such low quality services. Should be ashamed

title: Amjad

title: The most wonderful train staff ever!
content: The GWR train staff on the Truro to London route need some serious appreciation today. So my partner and I are off to Scotland this week for our first holiday in years and we had to come up the day before our flight from London by train. So we get to Plymouth and my partner suddenly realises he forgot to bring any photo ID with him for the flight. Cue panic mode. Not knowing what to do about our train tickets but knowing at least one of us had to go back for his ID, he went and asked the staff on board for help and they absolutely knocked it out of the park! Not only were they super calm and friendly and understanding, they helped him get back to Truro and get a seat on the sleeper train (this was the only next train back to London in time after he got to Truro) back to London for no extra cost. They even called ahead to the staff on the sleeper train to make them aware of his situation so they were expecting him on board and let him know he had nothing to worry about. GWR train staff are absolute stars honestly!!💖💖💖 Crisis averted and holiday saved 😌🫶 Thank you so much!!!!

title: Not the worst and they do some good stuff
content: Unlike my previous review of GWR pointing out the woefully inadequate excuses for delays, inability to run on time or at all, constant bickering between Operator and Network Rail etc., I thought I would commend them on their (few) good points:1. Staff - most make a real effort to do a great job cheerfully and apologetically despite regular shortages of colleagues, (overpaid) drivers etc. They do a good job under difficult circumstances. Thank you.2. Delay Repay - If you have not used this service you should as it works, pays out quickly and fairly, with minimal administration time. If only the Railway ran as efficiently. We can all dream...3. Delays - If the delay is short, they will attempt to make up the time i.e. 5-10 minutes. If it is over that they seem to slow down to ensure you can claim and make sure people know how to. Especially if it is a track or signaling issue, as I suspect this gets billed to Network Rail!? Thank you for putting Customers first in that respect.4. Ticket Inspections - The vast majority of people do pay and the inspectors are firm but fair, and will use good common sense and discretion if for instance someone is getting off at the next stop, made an error  in the purchase. 5. Completely messed up journeys - Again staff use a lot of discretion to get you home by whatever means, allowing travel pretty much on any train to get you to your destination and station staff go out of their way to be helpful. Well done.I don't think GWR are anywhere near the worst operator and think many of their issues are due to constraints with timetables, Network Rail and other Operators, over which they probably have little control. What they do have control over they do well.It's a shame the UK's rail service, the first and oldest in the World has become a frustration to users and an embarrassment compared to France, Germany, Spain, Switzerland, Japan etc. all of whom put the UK to shame.

content: Everyone should have the right to have a rest, especially on Sunday’s evening, yet there are some duties to deliver as a rail services for the price of £17 for a single ticket. I fully acknowledge the right of the GWR to change the transport/route/service at any point of the journey, but there should be a clear indication of how to get to the bus stop and most importantly which bus number should I have looked for.

What a bunch of crooks, how these people are allowed to run a public service that people rely on to get to work or go home is beyond belief. title: Poor sleeper experience
content: Writing a review about a recent experience that has already been written on here by another member of family. I recently travelled from London Paddington to Penzance on the sleeper service on the evening of Monday 16th September. As written on a previous review; I would like to extend my sincere and severe displeasure and disappointment at the staff working on the service that evening. The cabin supervisor had notified us that they were short staffed that evening but unfortunately that didn’t stop the staff who were working standing around in the walkways having loud conversations and laughing whilst myself, my Mum and others’ in that cabin were disturbed and woken up on numerous occasions. I am saddened to say that when my Mum approached these women to ask them to keep the noise down; they didn’t respond with any sympathy or any care at all. One woman even laughed at her and rolled her eyes as if she was acting like a hysterical woman. I can say that if I had approached these women as a big guy and asked the same, I feel their response may have been different. Regardless of whether that is the case or not, I am quite frankly hugely unhappy at how these women who are employed to make this sleeper service a pleasant and peaceful environment for PAYING customers’ to have a quiet nights sleep - have behaved all round. It reflects extremely poorly on GWR and having already had poor staff experiences’ with them in the past, I know that giving this feedback to them directly will be most likely ignored. You would expect this sort of behaviour from customers’ who are maybe unaware of the conditions and the nature of this service, but the fact this was staff makes this all the more unfortunate. I do know the first name of the supervisor of this cabin service and she is called Gail. She never made any attempts to rectify the situation or apologise for the disturbance these women caused us on our journey. So bear that in mind when booking this service.

title: Rubbish Mobile App, no option for ticket by email
content: I bought a ticket online for travel the next day. I was forced to register with GWR to do so. I used a password manager to generate and save a secure password. The only options were to collect tickets from the station or use the app. For some reason, emailing them to me was not an option. I was able to reserve a seat at no extra cost (the ticket price was pretty extortionate to begin with to be fair, given the train was about 2/3 full)I'm not the most punctual person at the best of times so, before bedtime I downloaded the app. I logged in, manually transcribing the long password. I don't have access to my password manager on my phone for security reasons. I checked I could access my tickets and then continued with my routine. The next morning I arrived at the station with about 7 minutes to spare. I opened the GWR app and was horrified to see I had to login again. Queue mad scramble to turn on the wifi hotspot on my phone, open my laptop, log back in to the app and access my tickets. I had to login again to get through the barriers when I arrived at my destination and then later that day for my return journey. I screenshotted the QR code to avoid having to do it a fourth time when I got home. On this occasion the train was on time and I was able to take advantage of an open return to get a flexible time slot for my return journeyI would be more forgiving of delayed trains as this is often beyond the operating company's control. The ticketing and mobile app user experience, which is infuriating, is completely within their control however, so if GWR wants a better review from me, they can work on this. For starters, just send me a QR code by email, I don't want a multitude of apps on my phone for services I only use occasionally. I can use a browser for those.

title: Awful. Don't waste your money on 1st.
content: If you watch the YouTube reviews of GWR First Class, they are almost unanimous in describing how bad it is – sadly I only saw those after making my booking. But even if I’d seen them first, I’m not sure I would have believed just how comically bad it is.First, when I bought my tickets in the app, I wasn’t given a seat reservation. When I tried to add this on the website, it gave me a reference number but not a seat. Ticket office staff couldn't help either, they just shrugged and said a ticket doesn’t guarantee a seat “and maybe there aren’t any available.”Fortunately there were, though only rear-facing ones. The service on the outbound leg was grumpy, with the catering guy being outright rude to the lady opposite who had trouble hearing him. On the return leg, there were no catering staff on board for the first hour – they only joined at a later station. They then said they’d misplaced the sandwiches from first class, and couldn’t transfer them from the standard class trolley without charging for them! Even the train manager couldn’t resolve this as “I don’t have the authority to do that” and “anyway catering isn’t guaranteed.”Oh, and the only time they serve complimentary wine in First is between 5pm and 7pm – outside of those two hours, you have to pay for it.So yes, the service is at least as bad as the reviews say. Don’t waste your money.

title: Disgusted
content: I don't normally book with GWR. However when I did they would not let me book an open return. On the return leg, I needed to come back 1 hr early. I asked at the gate whether I could come through and travel on the 3:20. Yes of course Madam. Please proceed. They even let me through the barrier. Halfway through the journey I have been charged £41.90. So no air conditioning, filthy toilets, no internet - worst than 3rd world country rail services. The train was half full so not in peak time. The glossy TV adverts are very different to the reality. Don't bother to book through a site that forces you to only be able to book advance singles for specific journeys. I wonder how many other people have been caught!

title: An improvement but still issues
content: Ok since my last review I have been registered as visually impaired which as you can imagine has made life a whole lot more difficult and one such difficulty I face now is using public transport.Things however have improved which is reflected in my 4 star rating but there are still issues which are a right pain in the rear end like for example the ridiculous positioning of plug sockets on trains now.They used to be between the tables and windows in an accessible location easy for anyone to reach but now they're between the seats which are a nightmare to not only find but also sitting with leads between your legs isn't a very comfortable ride.I've been on a couple of trains where the plug sockets were in different directions and I actually ended up with cramp in my back trying to get the plug into the socket because it wasnt obvious which way it was meant to go.My other issue is regarding ticket purchasing because when I request the quiet coach it's because I have sensory issues and want to sit in a quiet location free from stress and anxiety.The seats I had reseved on my last journey had been stolen by another customer so I ventured to find the quiet coach which when I reached it was anything but quiet as small children were running around, shouting, throwing things and it was hectic.So when customers request specific seats or carriages it's for a good reason and don't just put them in any location which could cause stress and physical discomfort.Anyway onto the positives.Whenever I've booked assistance to help me through the various stations I have visited etc it's always been first rate and the staff have always gone above and beyond the call of duty to help me so thankyou to them and I look forward to my next journey assuming they get my seat allocation right next time.

title: Rebrand to Worst Western Railway
content: After an unforgettable weekend at Glastonbury, my experience was topped off by a truly surreal performance from Great Western Railway. Picture this: I’m drenched, waiting for my train back to London in the pouring rain, and suddenly, I’m cast as the unwitting star in GWR’s latest drama—Revenue Protection: The Musical.The plot twist? I’m asked to produce my railcard in a place where signal is about as mythical as the Loch Ness Monster. Despite my best attempts to summon the internet gods, my app stubbornly refused to load. Cue 30 minutes of me trying to convince GWR’s finest that I did indeed possess a railcard, only to be rewarded with an impromptu reading of my “amendment rights” and a court summons—because nothing says “welcome home” like the threat of legal action.But wait, the show must go on! Another half hour later, the clouds parted, and I finally got enough signal to prove my innocence. With the railcard now triumphantly displayed, I returned to the revenue officer, hoping this farce might finally end on a high note. Alas, it was not to be.Fast forward four weeks, and I’ve just received a delightful letter in the post—another threat, this time featuring the possibility of court! GWR, I must applaud you. You’ve truly turned customer service into a comedy of errors, complete with all the drama, suspense, and absurdity of a Shakespearean tragedy. Bravo!

title: Last year GWR had severe delays and we…
content: Last year GWR had severe delays and we were held up at Bristol for over 2 hours followed by myself, whom is disabled and my friend whom was heavily pregnant at the time having to stand in a corridor with the passengers from two other trains, the return journey was no better.  After giving GWR copies of all tickets and booking reference codes they kept asking for the same evidence over and over, until I gave in and got no refund / compensation.Now I have just booked tickets for another trip to Wales, with the same friend and her two toddlers.  Yesterday the price was £144, with a Disabled Person's Railcard.  Now it went up to £181.60.  After bookingand logging out I accidently refreshed and saw a price of saw a price of £139.  So I closed the tabs, cleared the cache and did another search for tickets.  Without adding the Railcard the price is £134.  So are GWR the most Disabled unfriendly company in the UK?  I think so!  After robbiong us last year they also robbed us this year.  They are taking advantage of the disabled and overcharging them.  Other rail companies give the 1/3 discount for both the disabled person and the companion / carer, GWR only discount the disabled person and overcharge any others on the same booking.  Some companies even allow a carer to go free, such as the Thames Clipper boats, cinemas allow the carer in for free, GWR rips the disabled person and the carer off.  When we go next year I intend to get a Disabled Caoch card and take advantage on booking as early as p[ossible to get the best fare.  Apart from GWR losing customers they are driving them to use other modes of transport (cars and coaches) which adds to the carbon footprint whilst claiming they cut that very same thing.If you can, I would advise that you avoid GWR if possible, boycotte them and let others know how unfriendly they are towards Disabled people and even make heavily pregnant women stand when the guard stood next to her could have requested a passenger removes his / her bags from the vacant seat, of which there were many.  If GWR was a statutary body they could be accused of breaches of the human rights acts and tried in an International court for the treatment of the disabled.

title: Unreliable Trains, OK Service

Booking system rarely works. Size of train often smaller than planned, so very cramped. Fully functioning around 50% of the time, plus GWR do offer delay repay. Staff - 5/5The staff are generally very nice and patient with people clearly trying to get on an earlier train, etc. Value - 3/5Not sure how to work out if it’s good value, but it is on the edge of slightly painful.Other - 4/5Clean, has dual plugs under seat. Reliability being a key area make GWR incredible frustrating to use. Any other business run this way would be going bust soon, but hurray for monopolies. However, it could be worse.

title: Unused tickets due to cancellation by GWR but refused a refund.
content: I purchased advance tickets from Bristol Parkway to London Paddington and back for 14th July. I was attending the BST festival in Hyde Park with my 13 year old daughter.GWR cancelled our train (22:37 from Paddington to Bristol Parkway on 14th July) at short notice (due to staff shortages most likely due to them watching the England v Spain Euro final). This caused huge stress for me as it potentially left my 13 year old daughter and I stranded in London until the following morning.We did not use the return tickets and found another way home.Raised a claim for a refund, but GWR are refusing. Their reason is they said they advised people not to travel after 6pm on 14th July. For some reason they are implying this over-rides their own advance ticket refund policy stating:"8.1 Your ticket is non-refundable. However, if the train you purchased a ticket for is cancelled or delayed and as a result you decide not to travel a refund will be offered on completely unused tickets and you will not be charged an administration fee. "I purchased my tickets via the GWR website directly but had no alert, either via the app or e-mail, to say our train had been cancelled. The only way I found out was by checking the train departures online and getting worried when the 22:37 didn't appear in the list.My tickets were unused and were purchased more than 2 weeks in advance. Therefore no basis for GWR to refuse a refund.I've had to raise a Paypal dispute as the only option GWR have provided is to raise another refund claim and give themselves another few days to reply (and no doubt probably refuse my claim again).Update 30/07:GWR did not respond to my Paypal dispute within the 10 day window so I got a refund by default.GWR did not respond to my e-mail on 20th July to their GWR Feedback e-mail address, detailing all the details in my original review.Sent a mail to Jason Ness, Head of Customer Relations at GWR, on 22nd July, no reply.The level of contempt for customers is very clear to me.I only generally use Paypal for smaller companies I haven't dealt with before as it gives me an easier route to raise a payment dispute. Luckily I chose to do the same when buying my advance train tickets. I recommend, if you can, to use Paypal, or other payment provider, that offers an easy way to raise disputes.The only reason I have to use GWR is the monopoly they have. I will try and get a coach in future, where possible.

title: GWR is a brand name of FirstGroup plc…
content: GWR is a brand name of FirstGroup plc who hold a monopoly over all rail travel in South Wales, the West Country, the Cotswolds, across southern England and into London. They reported a £654 million profit for the last financial year and pay significant dividends to their shareholders.  The company charges much higher fares than the comparable average in other developed European countries but offers a markedly lower level of service. The company reinvests the absolute minimum into the service whilst extorting the absolute maximum in fares it can get away with from consumers. It often accomplishes this by relying on so called “revenue protection” legislation to threaten travellers with a criminal sanction to impose their will over any individual contractual disagreement. They do this, despite the fact that such rules were designed to address deliberate fare evasion and not to safeguard privately owned railway companies from the incompetence of their own staff. The train service itself is ludicrously unreliable with hourly cancellations, trains breaking down, signal failures and scheduled trains simply not turning up at all. To account for this, commuters are forced to try and catch the earliest and often the most expensive train as they cannot rely on a later scheduled train actually turning up to get them to work on time. If a customer does buy a ticket for a train they cannot use because it hasn’t turned up then they have to wait months for a refund. If they rationally decide to wait and see if the train turns up and attempt to pay on the train, then they are faced with the prosect of a £100 fine with criminal sanctions attached if they understandably refuse to pay this penalty fare. GWR stands for the Great Western Railway Company, which in itself is laughably disingenuous claim. The only thing great about a GWR journey is the relief you feel if arriving at your destination, on that rare occasion, without incident.

title: Quiet Carriage was not quite the right description!
content: After booking a single from Swindon to Hayle and paying over £100 for the roughly 4.5 hour journey, and pre-booking a "quiet carriage" seat, I was expecting a lovely relaxing "why not travel by train?" experience.My expectations were crushed within the first 20 minutes of sitting down.Far from being a quiet carriage, it seemed that the majority of the other passengers simply ignored the fact that the carriage is reserved for passengers that do not want to listen to hilarious YouTube clips or music with overly produced bass lines!As well as that, many of the passengers present were also taking personal and business calls.Despite several GWR staff members walking through the carriage throughout the journey, nothing was said or done to stop the behaviour.After raising a complaint with GWR, I must admit that I was expecting this forward thinking, customer focused company to respond with some form of recognition and perhaps some small amount of compensation, but instead received the following reply."To ensure we are acting within our compensation guidelines, we will not be offering any compensation on this occasion, and I hope your next journey with us is more pleasant."Wow.Good luck to GWR and their "compensation guidelines", which by the way, are an internal document and cannot be sent to me for viewing. I asked!If I could give zero stars here I most definitely would.Absolutely abysmal customer service.

title: Night Riviera (the Torture Train)
content: Came here to write a review on the awful changes by GWR - see that I’m not alone… good.Got the ‘night riviera’ from London to Penzance, a journey I last took and very much enjoyed about 15 years ago. I don’t know what happened to GWR in the interim, but see the corporate greed has taken over. It was the least comfortable train journey of my life by some distance. Where before they had plush reclining seats with ample room and thick cushions you could drift away on, they have thin, bolt upright, plastic, fixed seats. I don’t know if these seats were tested by sleeping beauty or another unconscious fictional character, or no one at all, because I couldn’t fall asleep on these chairs if I had 13 kilos of chloroform injected into my heart. If I was dead I would in fact muster the energy to get up from these chairs and lie instead on a comfortable bed of nails. Less a night riviera than a hellish torture train. I would love to watch a GWR boss take the train himself and see his reaction, if it was like anyone else in our carriage, I think he’d prefer to run naked through the Donbas flying a flag of Putin being buggered by Joe Biden, shouting Slava Ukraini. Not a single person got any sleep whatsoever, there are no modifications on this train to accommodate sleeping. In fact I would firmly assume someone has gone out of their way (as described above) to prevent people from sleeping on this sleeper train.Safe to say I’ll drive next time - shameful.

SHAME on you GWR it could of been a medical issue is this how you treat Disabled passengers leave them stranded and in a vulnerable situation.

title: Please improve.
content: I would give 0 stars if I could. My first experience with this train service was disastrous and left a lasting negative impression. Here’s why:1. **Cancelled Train with Poor Communication:** Our train was canceled because there were too many trains at the station. Instead of providing a clear, actionable solution, the company left us, their customers, to figure it out ourselves. This lack of responsibility and transparency is unacceptable.2. **Overcrowded and Uncomfortable Conditions:** We were forced to board another train heading to a different destination, and it was so overcrowded that we had to stand for hours. The situation was chaotic, with people constantly squeezing past to get on or off the train. This is not only uncomfortable but also unsafe.3. **Neglect of Vulnerable Passengers:** I witnessed several alarming situations:    - A person with a broken leg had to stand for hours because there were no seats available.    - Numerous passengers, including those with limited mobility, were left standing for the entire journey. This led to visible discomfort, with people experiencing cramps and fatigue.     This blatant disregard for the needs of vulnerable passengers is inexcusable and highlights a severe lack of empathy and planning on the company’s part.4. **Prioritization of Profit Over Comfort and Safety:** It is evident that this company prioritizes profit over the comfort and safety of its passengers. Their disregard for basic customer care and the well-being of their passengers is appalling.5. **Disregard for Feedback:** If this review gets deleted, it will only confirm my suspicion that the company is overwhelmed with negative feedback and is attempting to silence dissatisfied customers rather than addressing the issues.6. **Lack of Genuine Apology or Solutions:** I do not want an automated, insincere apology asking me to contact them. This service needs substantial improvement. They must start caring about their customers’ health, comfort, and safety.I will never use this train service again and strongly advise others to avoid it. This kind of negligent service should not be tolerated, and it is vital that they make significant changes to address these issues immediately.

title: Absolutely dreadful.
content: Absolutely dreadful. That's the only way to describe the abysmal service provided by GWR trains. For a company tasked with transporting thousands of people every day, you'd think they would have figured out the basics by now. Instead, what passengers get is an experience akin to a crowded cattle cart from the 19th century.First, let's talk about the overcrowding. GWR trains are always packed to the brim. It's as if they've made a concerted effort to fit as many people as possible into each carriage, regardless of comfort or safety. Standing shoulder-to-shoulder in the aisles has become the norm. Want a seat? Forget it. Even if you book in advance, finding a free spot is a herculean task. The trains are perpetually full, and GWR seems either blissfully unaware or blatantly indifferent to the problem.And then there's the issue of carriage numbers. One would assume that during peak times, a competent train service would add extra carriages to accommodate the increased demand. But not GWR. No, they seem to revel in running trains with half the carriages they should have. It's almost as if they enjoy watching the chaos that ensues as people scramble for the few available spaces. It's an exercise in frustration and futility, and GWR appears to have no intention of rectifying the situation.Punctuality is another foreign concept to GWR. The trains are always late. Not occasionally, not sometimes—always. Whether it's a short trip or a long haul, you can bet that your train will be delayed. This consistent tardiness throws plans into disarray, making it impossible to rely on their service for anything time-sensitive. They've turned what should be a straightforward journey into a stress-inducing ordeal.To sum up, GWR trains epitomize everything that can go wrong with public transportation. They're overcrowded, inadequately serviced, and chronically late. It's a disservice to the passengers who pay good money for tickets only to be met with such an appalling experience. One can only hope that GWR takes a hard look at their operations and makes drastic improvements. Until then, passengers will continue to suffer through what is undoubtedly one of the worst train services in operation today.

title: GWR runs empty sleeper berths despite on train demand.
content: GWR does not act in either customer or taxpayer’s interest.So, when the Night Riviera sleeper service runs with empty berths, GWR demands the maximum £150 to upgrade on the train, for a product that is advertised as starting from £34.This is because GWR are already being paid by Govt (us) to run the service with no revenue risk (as per their contract). Therefore, despite the cost of berths starting from £34 - which one might assume applies at times of low demand - they have no commercial or operational interest in selling empty berths on a moving train and providing extra revenue to the Treasury (us).GWR responded with guff about market rates - without spotting the many ironies in that argument.We all understand lastminute.com pricing versus early booking. Bearing in mind there is literally no risk to GWR at all - they could easily let on the spot passengers who already have a booked ticket pay more or less the advertised rate, and get that money back to the taxpayer.Another nail in the coffin of rail privatisation, if there’s any sense in the world.

title: Kind and Helpful Staff
content: I would like to pass on a big thank to various members of GWR staff who were all very helpful yesterday when I lost my mobile.Helen was on duty at Bodmin Parkway, where I alighted from the 09.34 from Camborne. Whilst we were walking around Lanhydrock, she kindly contacted Camborne, where a colleague checked the toilets to see if I'd dropped it there. When we got home, we were able to track my mobile and found it was still on board the train where it must have slipped out of my pocket. The train was on its return trip from Paddington due to arrive in Penzance at 20.10.We drove to Penzance where I explained what had happened to a member of staff who was just entering the station as I was. He listened attentively to my story and said he would return when the train arrived. At the same time a member of platform staff checked I was okay. The train arrived, and the staff member, who's name I hadn't asked,  boarded the train with us to search where we thought we'd been sitting. My husband called my mobile, and the member of staff was able to locate it under what must have been my seat in the morning.My mobile had spent nearly 10 hours, unaccompanied, on train travelling from Cornwall to London and back to be returned to me.Thank you GWR.Jo Rogers

title: GWR has failed to meet basic standards…
content: GWR has failed to meet basic standards of customer service and support. Recently, my daughter traveled from London to Bristol with a valid ticket and a 16-21 Railcard, only to face a distressing experience. Despite having the necessary documents, a GWR conductor insisted on seeing her photocard on the app, which was difficult due to poor signal on the train. In a coercive manner, the conductor threatened to involve the police and remove her from the train unless she purchased a new ticket on the spot. This led to her paying nearly £200 for a ticket she did not need, leaving her in tears and without adequate support.Following this incident, we lodged a formal complaint with GWR, providing evidence of the valid ticket and railcard. Despite assurances of an investigation, the company failed to respond to our follow-up emails, leaving us feeling ignored and frustrated. We have now escalated the matter to the rail ombudsman for a thorough investigation, accompanied by concrete evidence of the legitimate travel undertaken that day.Overall, the treatment my daughter received from GWR was unacceptable, lacking empathy and understanding. We hope that through the intervention of the rail ombudsman, justice will be served, and such situations can be prevented in the future. Traveling with GWR should not result in unnecessary stress and financial burden for passengers who have done nothing wrong.

title: Never go West or South
content: There’s a joke in our house “never go West”. It’s spawned from the fact that trains eastbound to London run on time, are clean, spacious and comfortable. These belong to South Western Railway. Go west and you’re lucky if 3 carriages turn up. It’s been like this for decades, hordes of tourists turning into sardines to visit one of 3 beautiful and popular cities called Bath, Bristol or Cardiff. I’ve now extended that saying, “Never go West or South” although unfortunately I have to regularly go southbound for work so I have no choice. The staff are typically great. But what the hell have they done with the carriages? You may as well give us planks to sit on. There’s no “luxuries” like somewhere to put a cup. You have to balance said cup between your knees and hope a severe scorching incident doesn’t occur. It does sometimes have patchy wifi and power sockets if that’s important to you. Now I can’t blame GWR for all the delays (of which there are many). People of Portsmouth and Southampton, reduce this risk, please behave yourselves; there are too many delays because of “passenger disturbances”. Get a grip.And if you were wondering there is no train North!

title: GWR abysmal service from management but train staff fabulous .
content: Gwr gets worse year by year. Or at least its management and train controllers do. I appreciate some things are outside their control but when delays are encountered now they seem to take planned  stations stops off at a whim and then they change it again and then today a third time in one journey . For the customers who don’t really know where they are and have to re arrange transport and lifts a numbers of times in a row it’s a nightmare . I have travelled up to london from Cornwall a few times recently and every single time they have been delayed significantly.  Today I’m on a train that has been delayed and stops taken off and people told to get off at Exeter. So we stayed on and then they decided to take even more stops off. Upon the second round of planned station stop removals we were advised to get off at Plymouth and catch the 18.21 instead, with no concern  shown it isn’t really the 18.21 because that in turn is delayed but they don’t mention that. Then something that is 100% in GWR’s control . The unreliable catering. It is so hit and miss and on last three legs the trolley wasn’t there or ‘they couldn’t get to all the coaches’. To travel four to five hours with no catering is abysmal and this happens to me on at least half my journeys all the time.  I feel for the poor staff who have to deal with grumpy customers , it can’t be easy for them and probably accounts for many shift absences. It was so easy when they had buffet cars. Other companies have new trains and manage it. Anglia have buffet cards AND trollies. I love travelling by train and have lived in many areas of the country but Gwr seem to have a knack of making travel miserable and frustrating.  They need to take a hard look at themselves and start putting their customers first and provide a better service than they seem able to. It’s getting worse every year. However as always the train staff are fabulous , the catering staff, ticket inspectors , train managers , they are all just brilliant but I feel for them where management, bean counters and train controllers, all of whom,  don’t have to face customers make all these decisions from behind the safety of a desk . Thank you to all the train staff doing such a fabulous job but as for Gwr train designers and buyers , senior managers and the train controllers it so often feels like a complete shambles .

GWR were a pleasure to travel with and I shall look forward to my next journey with them.

content: One star is too many. I often travel with GWR, not because I choose too, but because I have no other way of getting back and forth from my Central London university. Countless times have I been scammed, had to pay an extra fee to change my train to an hour later, after the extortionate fee I’ve already paid to sit on the stinky disgusting trains. This is just an example of how they’ve robbed my bank account. How do they get away with it? The trains are almost always delayed or cancelled. A few weeks ago, I had accidentally bought a ticket for the wrong time - my fault completely, however was totally an innocent mistake.  As I said, I attend university, hence not being famous for having extra cash to spare. The man told me I can either pay £80 for an ‘any time single day ticket’ or get prosecuted. I continued to pay which left me pocketless, I planned to spend the £80 on food and travel for the week. I had already paid £22 for the single ticket so that single, 50 minute journey cost me £102. I later did some research, a single any time day ticket is £55. Bloody scammers. GWR only get customers because it’s literally the only option we have. Needs to be changed, why am I paying so much money? What does the customers money go towards? It’s certainly not improving train quality, train punctuality or efficiency.I would rather die than travel with GWR. They’re lucky most of us have no choice. I despise these trains and get angry sat on them. F’ing scammers.

content: I use the trains most days of the week and you would think this would make my journeys stress free. The trains are late and not always for a reason thats out of their control, the expence of the tickets is a joke especally for the younger generation i have 2 jobs and go to uni i can barely afford just getting there. If GWR are messing their customers around like this then no wonder hardly anyone uses them and they will have to raise the prices this makes it unfair on customers that have no other option .I am gob smacked with how most of the staff treat people on the trains- I was 15 years old travelling by train alone becuse I couldn't buy at ticket at my local station as there was not a ticket machine or ticket officer they took £90 nearly all of my savings at the time. The train strikes are so pathetic it's the NHS we need to be worrying about and the millions of people that are being fu*** by the system, train drivers are fine being paid well above average. My blood is boiling

title: The difficulty with GWR is the staff a…
content: The difficulty with GWR is the staff a lot of the time. Read the many reviews. Delays are never good as are other issues that occur. With more actions like this GWR could improve overnight. Sadly I can only conclude that management are to weak to travel on the service themselves and take up issues when they come across them. Asking passengers to fill in a complaint form is really quite poor. My experience today was not good. We have been using the trains more frequently of late & I can understand why customer satisfaction is at a low level. I have been responsible for customer service of millions of customers and if the culture is not right poor outcomes are unavoidable. There is confusion in GWR as to who is the customer. content: I travel regularly on GWR trains and appreciate that certain things are out of their control. However when a train is delayed more than 15 mins we as customers are entitled to claims m delay repay. Every announcement advertises that fact. The procedure to claim is deliberately designed to make it nearly impossible for the everyday consumer to apply. It’s long winded, confusing and misleading. In my experience it has also asked me to sign in again taking me back to the beginning of the process hoping no doubt that I would give up. This should be looked at by a higher authority to stop all train companies paying back compensation that their customers are entitled to.

title: Unacceptable Service at a Premium Price: The Great Western Rail Maidenhead-Paddington Debacle
content: Paying over £4500 a year for the Great Western Rail (GWR) service between Maidenhead and Paddington should guarantee a seamless commute. Instead, GWR offers an experience that borders on the intolerable, blatantly disrespecting both the time and finances of its passengers.Punctuality is Nonexistent: GWR’s concept of timekeeping is abysmal. The routine delays and cancellations are a direct insult to any notion of professional commitment or personal time. The lack of communication during these delays only compounds the frustration, showing a blatant disregard for passenger convenience.Sardine Can Conditions: The overcrowded trains during peak hours are a clear sign of GWR’s failure to accommodate its passengers comfortably or even safely. Charging a premium for what amounts to a daily ordeal in cramped conditions is outrageous. The deteriorating state of the train interiors further demonstrates GWR’s neglect towards maintaining a standard of service.Customer Service is a Myth: Encounters with GWR staff, on the rare occasion they occur, have been utterly disappointing. Their indifference towards passenger grievances shows a systemic failure in training and customer service ethos. The robotic and impersonal responses to complaints are a testament to GWR’s disregard for its customers.A Gross Mismatch of Value for Money: The audacity to charge exorbitant fees for this level of service is astonishing. GWR appears to operate in a bubble, oblivious to the standards of value and service that customers rightly expect. This isn’t just poor service; it’s a comprehensive failure to deliver on basic promises.GWR’s Maidenhead-Paddington service is a textbook example of how not to operate a train service. We, the passengers, are not mere revenue streams but the lifeline of your operation. Our patience has its limits, and they have been thoroughly tested.Immediate and significant improvements are non-negotiable. GWR must take drastic actions to overhaul its service, focusing genuinely on enhancing the passenger experience. Until then, passengers have every right to question the utility of their investment and explore alternatives that respect their needs and contributions.To GWR: It’s high time to recommit to your passengers or step aside for a service that will.This version intensifies the critique, emphasizing the need for urgent action by Great Western Rail.

title: Excruciating seats & torturous overall rail-experience: This is the age of the pain.
content: GWR’s Hitachi trains give a ghastly rail-travel experience. 1) The terrible seats are surely the most uncomfortable seat on any train that’s ever existed.  Your posterior will be sat on a metal bar - that’s thinly covered with a layer of fabric; it’s like sitting on a rock.  The thin and far too upright back-rest is no better (seats in First Class are barely better; an utter waste of the extra cost).  You’ll be squirming and aching within 20 minutes. Evidently every expense and consideration for physical comfort has been spared by GWR. This is not my opinion; every fellow-passenger and GWR worker that I’ve ever spoken to agrees that the seating is horrendous. 2) The loud and CONSTANT tannoy announcements will frazzle your brain.  You can’t think without interruption (aside from the ongoing agony of your posterior and back) for more than a few minutes at a time, before you’ll again hear a set of inane, unnecessary, repetitious-to-insanity-producing announcements. 3) All year round the carriages’ temperature will almost invariably be too cold.  For whatever unfathomable reason, there’s seemingly a policy of ‘we’ve got air-conditioning in trains now, so let’s use it maximally’. 4) The harsh, blinding – interrogation luminosity – lights of the carriages at night will ensure you cannot relax, doze or sleep (even if you could do so miraculously through your bottom’s pain and ignore the tannoy).  5) The demise of the buffet car, and its replacement with the trolley service, is a sad, sad thing.  In addition to a notional buffet car motivating you from your stupor of discomfort to stand up and walk somewhere to try to ease your seat-induced aches, and warm up, the buffet car was an institution – for the opportunity it gave to chat to fellow passengers. 6) The water dispenser for washing your hands in the WC cubicles almost never works well or at all.  Thus back to your torture-seat you’ll stiffly hobble, with liquid soap all over your hands (until you learn to never pump soap until you’ve experimented firstly to see how bad, if at all, the water is dispensing).  You arrive at your destination, even after (hopefully) a short trip, aching from the awful seats, freezing from the temperature, brain dead from the tannoy, squinting with tiredness/eye-strain from the glaring lights, and with sticky hands.  GWR clearly holds its heritage and its customers with utter indifference...or even contempt.  For with these trains GWR could hardly have engineered a more unpleasant train-travel experience if they tried.  And GWR merely reply with words that would deny us - thousands of us - of our (very) painfully real experience; they’ll write such as “our trains’ seats are ergonomically designed and are supportive on long trips”; as if their hollow words magic-away the incontrovertible GWR-shaming facts, such as that of their seats being horrendously uncomfortable (for all trips) and so that of our bodies seriously aching from sitting on the back-breaking, bottom-agonising, presumably cheapest seats GWR could buy for their Hitachi trains.  This is the age of the pain.

title: Dire GWR Service
content: Of late, an utterly appalling service. Cancellations appear to have become endemic, are unexplained, and invariably without passengers being offered an alternative such as bus replacement. The reasons for the continual delays and cancellations seem never ending. Often cancellations are notified shortly before schedule service times. One suspects this is to ensure that as many persons as possible purchase tickets for a service that is not available to them. Station staff seem unable to offer apologies or empathise with what is often substantial inconvenience. It is as if the travelling public are an inconvenience. Why is it seemingly so impossible to run timely, clean, state of the art trains such as are enjoyed by the Spanish?   The problem is the travelling public soak up this dire service whilst there is little means to hold top management to account. I suspect that taking the Trans Siberian Express from Moscow to Vladivostok would be less of a challenge for the traveller than attempting a timely, uninterrupted journey from, say Newbury to London Paddington. However we will all continue to shuffle like so many lemmings onto these dire services when the inevitable price hike hits.  I suppose we just have to be grateful that any train is running. One of a number of reasons to emigrate.

title: GWR: Dreadful Service Gets Worse
content: I am shocked and appalled by the dreadful nature of GWR. They clearly believe they are a cut above the rest of us and have NO perception of what customer service looks like. Below is my copy of the appeal to the ridiculous penalty fare I was given. Today I received notification that the Appeal service have decided that I have missed the deadline to appeal and therefore they will increase the fine. UNBELIEVABLE. I could not Appeal as their system blocked me out as GWR Person had filled in their form incorrectly. Smacks of a money making scam from GWR. Who's service is appalling - making people late or not able to get places due to strike action. In my work commute I travel from Hungerford to Liverpool Street via train and tube.  As I travel on demand I buy tickets as required. There is no way to purchase the travelcard required for my commute from the machine on the station only a Anytime Day Return travel card which is more expensive.If time and queue allows it (there is only one ticket machine) I will purchase the more expensive option, otherwise I purchase it from the conductor on the train.  On this particular morning when attempting to purchase my ticket on the train from the conductor, I was told that he did not have a printer that printed the correct ticket.  Due to this the conductor suggested I could purchase the ticket at the ticket office at the barriers coming off the trains.  I'd note I've always purchased my tickets and never ride a train without paying.  I went to the ticket booth and got in line roughly 10th in the queue.  I was talking my 7 year old daughter on the phone whilst waiting when a revenue office pulled me from the queue when I was next up to purchase my ticket.  I assumed he had the mobile ticket machine like the conductors and was going to sell me my ticket as this does happen sometimes.  Instead the officer asked what I was doing, where had I travelled from and he then rudely informed me that I he was going to issue a penalty notice for not paying for my ticket.  I explained to him what had happened but he kept insisting that I was trying to cheat the system, which is categorically untrue.  At this point I told my daughter I had to hang-up as this rude officer was harassing me.  He accused me of abusing him, again untrue, (I had only called him rude for interrupting me on a call without even an apology), and threatened to call over the police.  I requested he did as it would be helpful to get someone capable of rational thought to explain this situation to.  But it was an empty threat and he continued to tell me he would write the penalty notice.  I tried to get one of the ticket officers to intervene as they see thousands of customers using this same approach to pay for their tickets when unable to purchase on the train.  Whist he agreed with me he could not intervene due to the fact the officer had already started to write the ticket (he did not have my details in which to do so, so he can’t have really got far).  After getting the notice I still waited in line and bought my ticket as I had originally set out to do. You can check the CCTV in the station as I'd assume we were in a place that would be recorded.  In fact I encourage you to review it, talk to the ticket office, and even the rude revenue office.  The story won't change, I was waiting to purchase a ticket at Paddington Station, as agreed by the conductor.  The officer was totally out of line and represents the type of bullying we frankly do not need.  I'd expect that the footage is reviewed and appropriate disciplinary actions are taken against him.Please note the time of this harassment was approximately 9 AM not noon as stated on the notice.I would appreciate your prompt review and expect the evidence of my statement, interviews of the ticket office, revenue office and of course the camera is surely enough to overturn this penalty.

For £70 i would expect more than a small square of dirty carpet and severe leg cramp. Still not my worst experience with the new trains...took the train to Reading a couple of months ago to go on a bike ride...LOL! The tiny broom closet bike storage was already filled with 2 bikes, which apparently is the TOTAL storage for bikes on the train. Kinda glad, watched someone struggle to get their bike out, which involves climbing practically into the cupboard to lift your bike up above your shoulders to hook it onto a tiny hook...no chance i would do that. I just stood in the aisle with my bike, fortunately train was again so busy people were standing as insufficient carriages were provided, so no-one could move even if they wanted to. Never getting GWR again, such as shame as the service was prompt and fast but a company run this incompetently, it's clearly easier to drive to a town on the outskirts of London, park and get the tube in. So much for 'let the train take the strain', more like 'let the train give you pain'. What idiot bought these new trains?

title: WARNING - GWR ARE FRAUDSTERS!!
content: I am writing this review so to warn other passengers of the abysmal customer service the Great Western Railway.On the 31/07/23 I went onto GWR website to book a ticket for 02/08/23 from Redhill to Swansea, I proceeded to the card payment section and entered all the details. However, after waiting a few minutes the GWR website advised me they were having problems with their site and I should try again later, I therefore cancelled and logged out understanding my payment had not gone through! Later in the evening I went back onto GWR website and this time was successful with payment being accepted and my booking made to travel on 02/08/23, I had an e-ticket which I travelled with on the booking date and as far as I was aware everything was fine.However, on 18 August I logged onto my bank account where I could see that 2 payments for the same amount had been taken from my account for the same journey!!  I immediately contacted GWR customer service, waiting 40mins to get through, to explain the situation and was informed by an unpleasant and indeed unhelpful customer service member that I had to wait 28 days or at least until the 28th of August to receive an automatic refund which she informed me was called a "ringfence payment" I was very sceptical that this would the happen but gave them the benefit of doubt  and waited until the 28th of August but to no surprise I did NOT receive my refund! I had no option but to waste another half a day trying to contact them to find out why I had not received the refund as previously informed!  After waiting another 55 mins to get through I did eventually speak to another advisor who was far more helpful and explained that the "ringfence refund" was not for my situation and she was going to log a complaint and request my refund for double payment for the same journey be refunded asap. I waited 10 days as I was advised it could take 7-10 working days for the refund dept to sort the refund  but I would definitely get a refund this time!! However, you can guess, no refund was ever received!! To my astonishment however, what I did receive was an email from a customer Support Advisor informing me that they only offer refunds on claims made within 28 days of the tickets expiry date and as it was now 11th Sept they would NOT be refunding me as it was over the 28 days!Double payment had been taken erroneously by GWR, they had given me incorrect information by way of the "ringfence payment refund" they had advised my to wait 28 days and again to wait another 7-10 days to receive my refund and YET they have the audacity to inform me they are not returning my money because I am out of time, not only is this unbelievable it is FRAUDULANT and I following trading standards advise I will be logging a formal complaint as advised, however, this does not deal with the distress and time wasted spent trying to get my money back which GWR should never have taken in the first place!!
