title: Poor Treatment of Customers on GWR Falmouth to Truro Route
content: I strongly dislike the way this company treats its customers, particularly on the route between Falmouth and Truro. The entire experience is consistently unpleasant. Their approach to customer service leaves much to be desired, as they manage to make passengers feel unwelcome and tense. The staff treats everyone as potential criminals until they provide proof of their tickets and railcards. It's a given that they will check your tickets and railcards without fail. If you attempt to purchase a ticket on board, you will promptly be scolded for not buying it at one of the smaller stations along the Falmouth to Truro route or online. If the company insists on policing everyone, it would make everyone's lives easier if they installed gates, clearly indicating that the only way to board is by purchasing a ticket in advance. Alternatively, they could at least put up some signs to inform passengers of the proper procedures.Recently, I witnessed an elderly lady, between 80 and 90 years old, attempting to buy a ticket on board. She was completely shocked to learn that she would be fined next time and that she must acquire a ticket prior to boarding. This is particularly concerning considering that some people only use their service once a year or may have difficulties with their memory. Additionally, the machine at the Penryn station is hidden from plain view, making it easy for passengers to forget to purchase their tickets. To make matters worse, there have been instances where the machine has food smeared on the screen, making it even more difficult to purchase tickets. These issues are clearly evident from the accounts of other unhappy customers. It's disheartening to see how the company makes its customers feel, especially considering that it has only been six months since they installed new machines and everyone is well aware of the strict ticket checks.Edit: Thank you for taking the time to respond and provide the link GWR. I appreciate your confirmation of the policy. While I understand and respect the need for ticket checks, I would like to emphasise the importance of a customer-friendly approach. It can be discouraging and stressful when customers, who have valid tickets and railcards, feel intimidated and stressed during the process.I have noticed that some passengers still believe it is possible to purchase tickets onboard the small service between Falmouth and Truro, which suggests a gap in communication. Installing ticket gates and clear signage directing customers to the ticket machines or online options could be effective in ensuring everyone boards with appropriate tickets.Continuing to make honest and paying customers uncomfortable may discourage them from using the service and potentially lead to them seeking alternative means of transport. Additionally, it could create a sense of hostility within the community.I genuinely believe that by adopting a more customer-centric approach, the overall experience for both passengers and staff can be greatly improved. Thank you again for your attention to this matter.

content: I now am uncertain of the role of a Train Manager; it is clearly not to help a passenger. content: Paddington to Maidenhead service is possibly the worst line I have ever experienced. Not sure I’ve ever arrived on time. The Maidenhead to Marlow service is great when it’s working. 10 mins late leaving today, 45 mins late getting in. Makes you wonder where the money from the constant price rises go. title: Diamond Employee
content: I have travelled on the 16.18 out of Paddington to Swansea today (16th May) and the back train manager/conductor (Sorry I didn’t get her name -Kind blond Welsh lady) is an asset to your organisation. She went over and above to ensure I made my connecting train to Carmarthen. GWR often comes in for much criticism but there are a lot of diamonds in the organisation. Thank you!!

title: Try getting a refund when GWR cancels a service...
content: GWR's cancellation of the Night Riviera Sleeper this week has plunged me into a dystopian nightmare, trying to get a refund on fares and sleeper reservations, not to mention connecting services. GWR gave me three days notice of the cancellation, but are refusing to refund four sleeper berths because I needed to apply more than seven days prior to travelling. It has also charged a £10 admin fee for refunding the fares, and a further £10 for cancelling a GWR connecting service. The refund procedure is awful, and there is no telephone help line. I will never, ever risk using GWR, let alone the sleeper again. I will get my refund if it takes going to the ombudsman, but it will take hours of effort. My advice is, steer clear.

title: Lauren based at Exeter St David is a credit to GWR, I hope she goes far
content: Lauren, based at Exeter St David, is amazing !!!Today, while doing her ticket activities, she moved my extremely hard case & then she carried it right over the bridge to the Paddington platform, then kept me company until she put it on the train.I was so happy l hugged her.Great employee !!!Got to add the refreshment staff on this Paddington train are lovely too.So very good travelling experience all round 😊

title: Major issues with both website & app, and inadequate customer service
content: Where to even begin? I lost 1,5 hours trying to book a London - Barnstaple ticket. Similar to the reviewer below (@Richard de Neufville), I got all the way to the end of the booking procedure, indicated my address, ticked all the boxes and pressed "Buy now". Nothing happened, the page just kept reloading, without giving me the possibility to enter my visa card details, and without any error message popping up either. I tried again multiple times, on two different browsers, unsuccessfully. I then decided to try to buy the tickets through the GWR app, downloaded the app, but as soon as I tried to enter London as my starting point I received the following error message: "We're sorry but we can't complete your request at the moment due to a technical issue, please try again later". I contacted Customer's service via the online chat, who was unable to explain what had gone wrong with the booking through the website. In the end, they found the explanation: the system blocked because it turns out that when you book from abroad (France in my case), you cannot choose the electronic ticket option, you have to collect the paper tickets at the train station. Aside from the absurdity and environmental impact of such a policy, it is nowhere indicated on the website, which does allow you to tick the option "electronic ticket". Customers' service was completely inadequate, and said the issue would be fixed very shortly. Three days later, nothing has changed on the website and the "temporary" glitch on the app has not been fixed, making it effectively impossible to book a GWR ticket.

title: The only consistency with GWR is how terrible it is!
content: I thought I had bought an advance first class ticket through Trainline for £62.95. This turned out to be a standard class ticket and was my mistake.The first class ticket was only £66.95. The utterly rude and unhelpful train manager then smugly told me that the on train upgrade was £90! How can such a price differential be justified? This was a demonstrable mistake that was clearly evidenced. The charge from GWR for the mistake amounted to being punitive. Particularly when there was no hot water, the train was running late (as usual) and multiple toilets were out of order. The trains are cheap and falling apart, the service is utterly unreliable. Ticket prices are far outside of the service and yet nothing changes. The service is almost comically bad.

title: Inflexible luggage policy and a very unfriendly member of staff
content: I arrived to London Paddington to catch an 8am train on a bank holiday Monday to Bodmin (Cornwall) with a 6 foot surfboard in a board bag. When I arrived to the gates, I was informed that the GWR policy states they don't allow surf boards. Now, despite this being the case, I was able to do this coming from Bodmin to Paddington a week before without any issue.When I arrived to the gate, a man (kindly) notified me that I couldn't take my board on the train but perhaps because it was quiet I could ask at the information desk and they'd make an exception. So there I went, and I spoke to another polite man who said the same thing: that it's against policy but perhaps because it's quiet the train manager would allow it.I then attempted to get back through the gates so that I could speak to the train manager, one of the staff at the gates was immediately unfriendly to me and told me that I couldn't go through and that I will not be allowed to board the train. After trying several times to politely ask if I could just go through and have a conversation with the train manager (as I had been instructed to do) he started shouting at me. I ignored him due to the fact he was being totally unreasonable and then went to back to the gate where the first member of staff (who asked me to go to the information desk) allowed me through. The extremely impolite employee, then came round and proceeded to shout at both myself and his colleague who permitted me to go through so that I could talk to the train manager. He then threatened to call the police to remove me because I was not permitted to be there - to be threatened like that was, quite frankly, a disgusting level of customer service. I ignored his threat and proceeded to find the train manager.I spoke with the train manager who, respectfully, employed his common sense and saw that my 6ft surfboard would fit in the bike storage of this practically empty train. I was then allowed to board the train and put my surf board in the storage (of which I have a photo - it's an empty bike storage with a 6ft board bag upright in the side, perhaps taking up 10% of the storage space).After being on the train for a few minutes, just before departure and just after I'd eaten my breakfast, the train manager came and found me and asked me to leave the train. It wasn't worth the argument and it was clear that the shockingly impolite employee had escalated the issue and made a big deal out of nothing. I felt as though he was purposely going out of his way to ruin my day.I got off the train and then as I walked back to the gates the impolite employee proceeded to raise his voice at his colleague who let me through to which point they got a manager involved to speak to the polite member of staff. I was then asked to leave and not be involved but I can't help but think what a sad, pathetic situation this is that the manager is talking to/perhaps disciplining the member of staff who was kind to me and tried his best to help out a customer  despite a nonsensical arbitrary policy which says I can't bring a surf board on an empty 8am train. Instead of this incredibly rude man who repeatedly raised his voice at both me and his colleagues and was nothing but unhelpful, unfriendly and unreasonable.I then had to get the tube with my board to London Waterloo where I caught a train with SW trains to Exeter St. Davids and then ask my girlfriend to drive 1.5 hours to come and pick me up. A huge inconvenience to both of us.Not being able to take a 6ft surfboard in a bag on an empty train that would have made no difference to anyone's journey and only served to completely ruin my day - what a ridiculous policy. It should be at the train manager's discretion. I purposely got up early and caught a super off peak train because I wanted to ensure it wasn't any hassle.The fact that every member of staff had to deflect the decision of permitting me onto the empty train with my surfboard to someone else makes me question how GWR treat their employees. I would perceive this as there existing a work culture where your staff members are discouraged to use their common sense and initiative in favour of upholding your inflexible, nonsensical policies to avoid being disciplined. I truly hope nothing has jeopardized the career of your polite employee and that you read this and consider changing your policy to something more flexible. Perhaps you could also consider identifying and educating the impolite employee on what is considered acceptable customer service.

title: Totally impossible to use GWR website…
content: Totally impossible to use GWR website to buy ticketsGot all the way to end, set up international address, checked all the boxes, pressed “buy now” System never proceeded !!Tried several times from scratch no luck at all.. AND NO EXPLANATIONTHIS SITE IS CLOSEST TO WORST EVER

title: Terrible at refunding. Useless app.
content: Trains are fine. I travel Bristol-London at least twice a month and delays are common. I can live with that, but what really annoys me is how difficult it is to claim a refund for a delay. I have no doubt GWR are very happy with this situation. Perhaps they would be willing to publish how much is saved for shareholders due to unclaimed refunds?I had a go using the GWR app to see if they had brought it into the 21st century. How hard can it be to figure out that if I have a ticket for a specific train which is then delayed, the refund should be automatic?But no, one has to go through the clunky claiming process.I am set up with Delay Repay but have never received a notification from it.The app is still pretty rubbish in all other respects. Trainline is still a better option.

title: GWR need to improve
content: I travel frequently on GWR. Roughly 1/3 of all my journeys are late (particularly the more long distance ones to London), sometimes even cancelled. There's multiple issues with GWR. Where do I start. It is quite clear that this company doesn't provide enough care for their staff. I heard this from the horses mouth only yesterday from someone within the organisation overhearing my partner's displeasure with the train service, and we were given all the real reasons why. Insufficient staffing, the closing of kiosks, track maintenance issues, several companies are involved in the participation to keep the railway track together rather than one consolidated rail service, no pay rises for the last 4 years etc (the list goes on). Morale is at an all time low. Customers want to speak with real people; whether it's on the train, or at the train service. Stop closing the help desks and making staff cuts. As a customer it is incredibly difficult to claim a refund. I use the trainline app in most cases and the app deletes my ticket. Most of the time I have to have a printed off ticket, and I provide this ticket for friends and family that I pay for to use the service. If that person doesn't keep the physical copy of the ticket, and a train is delayed or cancel, you cannot get a refund. Despite the organisation has full proof of the transaction and the code etc (which I can forward) Why is that? Surely that's proof enough?The UK needs to nationalise the railway service in my opinion. It's evident that private companies don't have a handle on the situation.

title: 3rd class treatment with a 1st class interrail ticket!
content: Be aware, if you travel on GWR using an interrail ticket (including seat reservations) and get delayed (more than 60 minutes) plus incur extra costs trying to make up for lost time you're entitled to nothing despite the train guard telling to claim on delay repay.  Alot of work claiming to get nowhere.

title: One of the few reliable train operators in the UK
content: I am lucky to live in a region where GWR operates, literally the best rail operator in the UK. I was in Bournemouth last weekend, got on an SWR train to get a transfer to Guildford, and it was totally fatal. I got off at Southampton and was so relieved to see a GWR train that goes to Bristol Temple Meads. Other operators such as SWR and Cross Country are just not reliable, with bad timetable management (e.g. stopping every 5 minutes on a direct train). Overall, the trip was very nice and the train ride was comfortable with kind staff. I then got into Bristol Temple Meads and got on a train to London Paddington, the train was comfortable and is a chill ride overall. This is how train rides should be like in this country, GWR is a good example for other operators to follow, absolutely amazing experience.

title: Cancelled Train & Refused to Refund
content: ** In response to GWR - you do not state what your WhatsApp, Twitter or Facebook contact details are.  In any event, I do not use Facebook, Twitter or WhatsApp... so your Customer Service continues to be useless.What Happened...Our train was an hour late leaving the station and then terminated altogether before our intended stop.  The train manager was most apologetic and advised we could get a full refund plus the cost of a taxi etc required to get us to our destination.  However, when we applied for the refund and costs it was a completely different story.Our first refund request was rejected with a short email that stated refund “unsuccessful”.  There was no reason provided.When I complained, an agent said they would look into it and asked for more evidence which I provided.A week passed and I heard nothing more… hence this bad review.To date, GWR have simply washed their hands of the fact they failed to provide the service I paid for and have actually incurred me additional costs.I feel like I’ve been robbed.GWR trains are, in my experience, frequently overcrowded.   Why is there no regulator to ensure safety on trains? If you must travel via GWR, book with The Trainline who have an exceptionally good and easy refund policy.  GWR do not appear to want to refund their passengers at all.

title: First time back on a train in a long…
content: First time back on a train in a long time. Last 3 trips cancelled due to strikes. Thought I would give it another try....0914 Worcester parkway to New Street. 5 of us. Train was packed before we got on. 2 Carriages. Horrible. Granddaughters having to stand all the way.

title: App requires further development to improve customer experience and refunds process needs reviewing
content: App takes time to load digital tickets and there have been cases where the tickets haven’t worked at barriers due a technical issue. Don’t like the fact that if a train is cancelled, you can’t get a refund on a ticket paid for through the app/online from the teller at the station. Need to have bought a paper ticket to get refund from teller. Don’t like the fact that you have to set up separate login details for GWR ticket refunds. Why not integrate refunds into the single online GWR account already set up to buy tickets in the app? That way, if there are cancellations, already frustrated customers don’t have to become more frustrated going through the long winded process of logging into the separate GWR Refunds website that also crashes on you whilst you’re providing all the proof requested. Also, again on the GWR refunds website, if you already have a ticket reference that you can only obtain after purchase, why ask the customer to upload the actual ticket also? What’s even more frustrating, after you’ve finally managed to go through the long winded refund process, you get a message at the saying “we will typically respond to your claim within 28 days”. Reduce this period to an acceptable 3-5 working days. The customer pays you there and then to buy the ticket but then due to an error in your train service, it takes nearly a month to refund the customer? Now the customer must bankroll GWR whist finding alternative transport. It’s not often that train services are cancelled but when they are, an already frustrating situation is made even worse by how GWR deals with these situations. Why not provide a better experience as per feedback above and have returning customers that’ll be happy to use your services again?

title: Worst train station I’ve ever been to
content: Worst train station I’ve ever been to, horrible employees. I’m glad I don’t have to use their service as often as I used to. Waste of money.

title: Wrong station
content: Whilst travelling on business last Wednesday there was a mix-up and I was dropped at the wrong station for my return journey home, and without enough time to reroute to the correct station.Had this been my local network it would have been a customer service ordeal and I would have likely been pressed into purchasing extra tickets.I was pleasantly surprised to find that this wasn't the case at Bristol Parkway Station.. Graham promptly modified my journey with no fuss, gave me directions and had me home earlier than my original route.

title: provide the service we pay for!
content: Why are there so many 5 carriages services at rush hour in the evening? You know how many people want to use the service, so why on earth can’t you provide enough carriages so people might be able to travel? The situation is so bad, that we are not talking about people having seats, we’re talking about there being enough space for people to squeeze in and stand up! Given that the tickets cost hundreds of pounds, do you think this is any where near acceptable?

title: Compassionate customer service
content: My wife was unable to travel for medical reasons and despite her claims being out of date (as more than 28 days had passed), Lucy in customer services refunded several journeys and was very kind. We're grateful for the compassionate service that she received. Thank you!

title: Had to sit on the floor while heavily pregnant.
content: My return train was cancelled from London to Plymouth, I tried to get on the next one as many others did, the train was packed, as in no one could move around. It was terrible. People standing and sitting through every single carriage and corridor. I was heavily pregnant and had to sit on my suitcase for 2hrs of the journey. I told the GWR staff that I was pregnant, he tried to get on the train and find me a seat but he couldn't even get into the carriage and admitted there was nothing he could do. I tried to get a refund, this was their response; "Due to your service being removed and you boarding another service, your seat reservation is no longer valid as once your service is cancelled, any bookings/requests made on this service is also cancelled. We cannot transfer bike or seat reservations onto the next services. This is to avoid disrupting passengers who have booked on this particular service. This is also to avoid double-booking seats. Due to your service being cancelled, your seat reservation was also cancelled. I see you mentioned you were pregnant. We have "priority seats" which is available for customers who require a seat more than others. If these seats have already been occupied by other passengers who also require them, we cannot relocate these passengers as these seats are first come-first serve". Thank you GWR for your top notch service.

title: They charge too much and are unreliable
content: So usually get the 5,48am train to avoid the exorbitant cost...(as their charging amounts are mental, and make me want to move to london)... get there and the train doesn't exist anymore, and the 6am one is delayed...so sat on a freezing platform for 45 mins now.Found out the pre6am train is now 5:36 or somthing... makes me honestly depressed with my life at this point.

title: Huge range of excuses for being LATE.
content: They waste their money installing speakers informing you that you are arriving to the end of the escalator.They are almost always late.GWR provides shameful services at luxury branded prices.Absolutely appealing.

title: The most uncomfortable seat
content: I use the train on a frequent basis from Cheltenham to London. It stops too frequently before Swindon with an idiotic reverse journey over to Gloucester. On many occasions, it saves me 45 minutes by driving to Swindon to get a train from Bristol to London. At least a few services should run direct to Swindon, maybe stopping once at Stroud. It is far too slow. On a positive, I always find the staff excellent. I have suffered cancellations, but usually for reasons beyond GWR control (incidents on track) and the refund process is swift and painless. Sadly you cannot say the same for the new Hitachi trains. They are awful. Could anyone design a more uncomfortable seat? You are sitting on a block of wood. I miss terrible the old HST trains. They might have been 40 years old but had more space and were far more comfortable. As a passenger, the new trains are a disaster.

title: Booked first class Exeter to Cardiff
content: Booked first class Exeter to Cardiff. No benefits whatsoever. Train was virtually empty and no buffet car. No drinks or food provided for 3 hour journey. Response from customer services was sorry but tough luck basically. Don’t bother.

title: Shambles

title: Steve the guard is fantastic

title: Good
content: Usually not delayed, quite clean and comfortable

title: GWR 1st Class
content: GWR 1st Class: On entry to the carriage, seats and floor were not spotless, and an empty water bottle had not been cleared from the table from the previous journey. Complimentary sandwiches were not on offer, over a 5 hour journey, due to the Easter weekend and sandwich suppliers not working or something. However, staff were pleasant and apologetic about this, and certainly not at fault: there is no promise of any catering delivery in the Ts & Cs anyway, where external factors are a cause; but they do their best. For some reason the staff were a lot chirpier on the return Penzance to Paddington journey, and very nice. Trolley service to seat was frequent, decent and friendly, with generous complimentary tea, coffee, biscuits, crisps, nuts, water etc. Good, comfortable solo window seat, affording nice views of the Cornish, Devonian and Somerset countryside. Both legs of the train journey ran like clockwork.I go 1st class if the ticket price is favourable, and to mitigate against the risk of a busy, noisy and cramped Standard class carriage. It depends on what you pay for a 1st Class seat, as to whether it's worth buying/upgrading to it. I'd use GWR 1st class again as it was sufficiently good for me.

title: Delay repay will normally just waste even more of your time
content: Applying for reimbursement for delays is a lengthy process and most of the time they refuse anyway without explaining why.

title: Utterly useless

The seats are like sitting in wooden boards with no back support and they are bolt upright. GWR WINS ALWAYS), the iron seats on the GWR class 387 are a little bit hard, perhaps add a little more padding?!?No one was in the train, I had so much space, incredible views. title: Expensive for a constantly poor service
content: I pay 10.10 everyday, with a railcard from Eggesford to Exeter. Every single during the train is packed with people standing through the isles and sitting on the floor. Not good value for money at all and the prices just keep getting higher and higher!!

title: Did not even want to give the a star
content: Did not even want to give the a star. Rubbish company always taken money for admin fee when you request a refund.

title: FIRST CLASS FARE NOT WORTH IT.
content: Just travelling back from Penzance and after spending £500 on 2 first class return tickets, was totally shocked that you get very little for that!On LNER and Avanti you at least get free food (even a full meal on LNER) and alcohic drinks and the fare is cheaper even though the journey is further.All GWR provide is 25 free sandwhiches for a 306 mile trip with 15 stops en-route. So when you ask for one, nothing is availabe. The staff were very nice and said they have complained on many occassions but nothing improves. Having to pay extra for food and drink is not value for the £500 spent.

title: TICKET DRAMA
content: Myself and my friend brought our return tickets from the machine at the Weston Super Mare station to Bristol Clifton  23rd March 11:00am, we were chatting so just took the first tickets that came out of the machine and carried on to get a drink.  When we were on the train the young man Jacob Bowles ask to see our tickets and my friend got out the two tickets that we had only to discover that we didn’t wait long enough at the ticket machine for it to continue to print the rest of the tickets, we had proof that we paid on the bank statement, Jacob came back and gave us a receipt to say that he had seen proof that we paid so we could continue our journey and also get the return journey, he went out of his way to help us, so would just like to say thank you and excellent customer service from Jacob Bowles

title: Fantastic service
content: I'm a carer and today I took a client on a shopping trip from Axminster to Exeter. With all the negative reviews I thought it would be good to leave a positive one. The man at Axminster helped with the parking ticket and all the information I needed for the trip with my disabled client. He and all the staff we encountered were so helpful, kind and happy. Getting on and off the train, we were helped with ramps and kindness. Thankyou all very much.

title: Inefficient, late and EXPENSIVE
content: What to say about this train operator? Frequent delays and cancellations, short carriages meaning you have to stand in the corridor for hours and VERY Expensive.

title: Waste of time submitting a claim as they do not refund for delayed and/or cancelled train journeys
content: 11:28 journey on 14/03 from London Paddington to Didcot Parkway was cancelled due to overhead wires, my journey ended up being delayed by an hour so I was advised to submit a claim using their Delay Repay process. They will not refund as they deny that the journey was delayed which does not make any sense. Waste of time and poor customer service.

title: Their trains were late and that…
content: Their trains were late and that qualified for a partial refund and they said they were 2 minutes late basically lying out of their backsides instead of the 17 odd minutes late and told them view the cctv and no response absolute helmet’s

title: Travelled from Newcastle to Penzance…
content: Travelled from Newcastle to Penzance 17/03/23 changed at Taunton (arrived 18/03/23). More often than not overcrowded and incredibly, intimidatingly noisy - felt very vulnerable and not at all safe. At one point in the journey (Cheltenham) we were all warned that the train was going to be packed with people leaving the racecourse - oh my god - if you know this already then you need to either limit the number of people getting on or lay on another service.  Gangways and exit routes completely blocked. Final incident, just after Plymouth, involved a number of people in drink/drugs fighting. It was a very violent incident with one member of the warring group already prepared wearing a stab vest. I feel sorry and concerned that staff have to deal with such situations and it begs the question why allow people to travel if they are not fit to do so. title: Compensation claim through Delay Repay - constant road blocks
content: When the GWR service I was on recently was delayed, the conductor announced that we were eligible for compensation and we should apply on GWR’s Delay Repay. Grand announcements indeed, which don't match with the reality of the system, which seems set up to keep successful claims (even legitimate ones) to a minimum. My return journey from Newton Abbot (NTA) to London Paddington (PAD) on 5 December was delayed by about 34 minutes on arrival. (scheduled departure: 12:55, actual departure: 13:14; scheduled arrival: 15:29; actual arrival: 16:04). So, I go to Delay Repay to make a claim but it was rejected because I submitted my booking summary (downloaded from my "Past bookings" in my GWR account, which had the booking ref but not the ticket - but that was the best I could do. GWR’s “Action Required” rejection email said: “Please provide a photo or scan of your travel ticket(s).”  The problem is: (a) the email confirmation from GWR did NOT attach a PDF of the ticket (like it was supposed to); (b) the QR codes with the ticket numbers on the booking have since been wiped from the app (apparently, the app erases them once the journey has taken place); and (c) "Past bookings" in my GWR account shows the booking reference and date of travel but NOT the TICKET NUMBER. I even went to the Paddington ticket office and spoke to a supervisor to ask for assistance, but he said they couldn't print a duplicate copy of my ticket because what I had bought was an ADVANCE TICKET. This supervisor was sympathetic to the fact that my ticket on the app had been wiped by itself and that the email confirmation had no PDF attachment. He even looked up the online schedule of train delays and confirmed that this train (No. 1A84) from NTA to PAD on 5 December was indeed delayed, and assured me the information was verifiable in the system. Fortunately, before the trip, I had gone to Paddington to change to an earlier train for the return journey (NTA-PAD). The person at the Paddington ticket office was kind enough to write down the ticket number (starting with A-xxxxxxxxxxxx) on the back of each seat reservation stub. Thankfully, because of that, I do have the A-xxxxxxxxxxxx number, but it is handwritten and not printed on a ticket.So, I scanned those seat reservation stubs with the handwritten ticket numbers and submitted them on Delay Repay. But I got a rejection again. The “Unsuccessful” email said: “Your claim has been checked using a set process and the details of any delay verified using industry systems holding historic train running information. We have reviewed your claim and can confirm the following: … Decision: Unsuccessful.”The fact is the train conductor on the NTA-PAD service scanned my QR codes when doing ticket checks, which should prove that my partner and I did indeed travel on that particular train on that day, on that particular booking reference. With all this being electronic, the information is there and verifiable. What is in theory a straightforward process is made impossible by the fact that: (a) Delay Repay insists on having the ticket (not just the booking reference); (b) GWR's email confirmation failed to attach a PDF of the ticket like they claim it did. The “Action Required” system-generated email saying that I needed to produce a copy of the ticket stated "A PDF of the ticket(s) purchased should have been emailed to you." Well, "should have been emailed" isn't the same as it actually having been emailed! (c) the app wipes out all QR codes and associated ticket numbers after the journey has been completed; (d) our past bookings in our GWR account only provide the booking reference but NOT THE TICKET NUMBER! B-D above show how impossible it is to get hold of the ticket. Why insist on us producing it when you are so keen to erase all record of it? I suspect this is designed to make the process difficult so as to keep GWR's compensation payments to a minimum. I also wonder if the non-PDF-ticket bearing email was on purpose so we couldn't produce a ticket to make a claim.Another fault with Delay Repay is that it doesn't have a box for explanations. It only accepts a scan of a QR code or upload of an image/PDF. There’s no way for one to tell them “I can’t provide the ticket because of X” (though I suspect it's set up that way on purpose). GWR customer service repeated the same lines: that the email confirmation should have a PDF ticket attached (no, it didn't!) and that I'd be able to obtain it from my GWR account (again, no!). Those purchasing advance tickets online should bear in mind that the QR code & ticket number disappear from the app once the journey is complete. Print paper tickets at the machines so you have a hard copy!And beware the Delay Repay sham!

title: Bullied by staff at Paddington station
content: On 28 July 2022, I was subjected to degrading and upsetting behaviour by a GWR staff member.I was unable to scan my eTicket to leave the platform side, so I queued up to get help from the GWR staff member.At least one customer pushed in front of me. The GWR staff member allowed this to happen. When I came to the front of the queue, another customer, who had been idle and allowed several customers to go before them, suddenly berated me for pushing in front. I apologised for not noticing this customer.When I approached the GWR staff member for help with my ticket, I was told to scan it. I tried to explain that I'd already done this but the staff member was disinterested.When I unsuccessfully scanned my ticket a second time, the GWR staff member finally decided to do something to help me progress. Unexpectedly, the staff member decided to put on their glasses to carefully inspect my eTicket, something which they did not do for other passengers with ticket scanning issues.When I passed through the ticket barriers, the GWR staff member berated me for pushing in front of the previously-mentioned customer. Given that other customers had pushed in front of me without challenge, I found the GWR staff member's intervention to be nonsensical and upsetting.When I approached the station helpdesk to raise a complaint, I was instructed to re-approach the GWR staff member I wanted to complain about in order to raise my complaint. I challenged this but was told again to do as instructed.I re-approached the GWR staff member to advise that I wanted to raise a formal complaint against their conduct. The GWR staff member appeared indignant and stormed off to get another member of staff to take my complaint. I could hear raised voices behind the ticket barrier wall.When I raised an online formal complaint against GWR and their staff, I waited over 4 weeks to receive an acknowledgement of my complaint.GWR failed to offer any compensation for the experience I had with their staff. This was because they "don’t offer compensation for staff complaints".I decided to take my formal complaint to the Rail Ombudsman. GWR decided to offer £25 in rail vouchers as compensation. I declined, because I did not value my upset at £25 and I did not want "store credit" for a company I am actively avoiding.---If GWR employ staff like the one who bullied me, with that person possibly being a supervisor, then it speaks volumes about the calibre of people that GWR employs.Needless to say, I do not recommend GWR (Great Western Railway) to anyone.

The air conditioning is not  working and there is no way to purchase water, for a 4.5 hour journey this is unacceptable and dangerous. If an emergency was to occur, it would be a tragedy as there is absolutely no way that ANYONE can access emergency points. There is no food carriage, or any way to purchase water. There is no justifiable reason for this horrific journey. GWR are opportunistic, greedy and do not care for their customers safety one bit. I think that everyone on this journey should receive a full-refund for this journey and GWR should stop exploiting there customers, by regulating how many tickets are sold.

content: GWR's handling of "delayed payments" which are due to customers following delayed train journeys is a scandal. title: Chasing a refund for 3 months and counting
content: My train was cancelled so I had to take the following train. On my journey to my destination I received an email telling me I could claim a refund. When I tried to fill out the form it wasn't working so I reached out to GWR via Twitter to ask for help - which I have proof of. On my way home I tried again and the website was working so I connected to the train's WiFi and filled out a form, in fact I have a screenshot of the compensation part of the form.I then set a reminder for 1 month to check on the progress of this refund.1 month later I reached out via Twitter to ask when I would receive my refund.I was told no refund had been logged to "clear browser cookie and cache" and try again again, but by this point I learned it was over 28 days which is the GWR time limit for applying for a refund. The agent telling me to clear my cache makes me think that this might be an issue they've experienced with other customers, that my claim was correctly submitted but that something went wrong in their end, particularly because the website wasn't working a few days prior to me submitting my claim as I know for 100% that I filled the form in. I have been trying to fight this case with GWR since May 24th and its still going on because they take so long to respond, and the gaps are getting further apart - 3 days, 5 days, 8 days, 24 days and now 5 days and waiting.. - it's ridiculous. And each response is restarting the conversation from scratch, dragging it out further, perhaps to make me give up? I won't. I've now reached out to an Obudsman to look into this case and their refund practices. My advice to others would be to keep a close eye on the progress of your refund and reapply/reach out long before the 28 days end to check on the progress of your claim. Going through these reviews, I see many others have very similar situations which I plan to share with the ombudsman and I reccomend you do the same!

title: Excellent customer service
content: Freddie, the train crew member on the 11:04 service from Paddington to Plymouth 28th June was excellent. He is to be congratulated for his great customer service skills.

title: Left Stranded very disappointed
content: Very disappointed with @GWRHelp they sold us a ticket from London Paddington to Bristol Airport. This includes charging us for a connection shuttle bus from Bristol Temple Meads. The train arrived at BTM 23:40 and the shuttle bus supposedly would arrive 23:50 and every twenty minutes after that  however after waiting one hour and being stranded at a very precarious spot we found out the bus did not run in the early hours and we had been wrongfully sold a ticket for that bus. We were slightly lucky as we were a couple but they had also done the same with a single female and a 18 year old exchange student. We eventually had to get a taxi as we would miss our flight, we have tried to claim but @GWRHelp declined to help and have not accepted responsibility for there misleading sale! We always use GWR but on this occasion we are very angry and upset that they have treated their paying passengers like this. Please please please be very careful especially if you are travelling on your own when booking this particular journey. We will think twice about using @GWRHelp again and will be contacting the @RailOmbudsman for further assistance

title: GWR do everything they can do avoid refunds
content: We had to cancel a journey due to illness (thankfully not covid).  Standard return, not advance tickets.   The GWR website would only allow me to claim for one section of the journey.  Having taken over three months to respond I was informed that my refund was only partial as I had failed to declare I wanted both segments refunded, that they were charging a £10 admin fee per claim, and that time had now run out to claim for the other segment.  All responses received (after the three month wait) have been curt and unhelpful.  Sadly unable to give zero stars otherwise would have done.

title: My fave trains
content: Date of experience: June 24, 2022

title: Sat 18 June
content: Sat 18 June - 12:24 Swansea to Paddington arrived at Swindon station 10min late with only 4 coaches and absolutely packed. Passengers standing in the doorways as no more seats, we could not get on the train and had to wait for next train 15min later. Next train arrived with a few empty seats. Sunday 19June, 12.21 Paddington to Swansea - our ‘Reserved seats’ (LOL) we’re taken by 3 young ladies from the Valleys of Wales, even with the seat signage clearly indicating the seats were reserved. When mentioning they were in our seats they just replied ‘well someone sat in our seats, so took these’. They refused to move and we managed to locate separate seats for the homeward journey.What is the point of GWR offering seat Reservation if it’s a free for all and no enforcement? Really poor service, next time we’ll take the car!

title: Absolutely disgusting
content: Absolutely disgusting, train from Taunton 6 mins late, 10 mile journey starting at Taunton! Aircon not working in any carriage, 40+ and no openable windows. Home journey, again (almost always) late and need to change platforms. Sh!t hole state of train.

title: If I could give zero stars I would
content: If I could give zero stars I would. Always try to avoid traveling GWR. Great Waste of Resource more like. Waiting 50 minutes for a train, train suddenly cancelled because tracks are too hot…then suddenly that train becomes a London bound train. I think 7% of GWR trains I’ve ridden were on time. Quick to fine, over charge and blame others but radio silence when ever they mess up. If you are looking for uncomfortable, cancelled, late trains and a rotten train company to the core - go with GWR. Would rather horse and cart than give my money to this rubbish.

title: If you have to cancel you may be in for a long wait for a refund and the process is fiddly
content: Update: After weeks of worrying, wondering whether I’d get my hundreds of pounds back, I got an automated email this morning saying my refund (less the admin fees they take) is on its way. Therefore I’ve given them an extra star because someone got to look at my case and they made the right decision behind the scenes for which I’m really grateful. No response to my complaint other than to direct me to the refund portal. You can’t win them all! 😂Previously:Bought tickets for the sleeper train from London to Penzeance, for my partner’s 50th, but now can’t go. Told GWR in plenty of time (nearly 3 weeks’ notice) - cabins sell fast, so there’s no reason they couldn’t put them back up for sale. Response to my refund request - no refund. No explanation, just no refund accepted. £400 down the drain. On their website it says they will refund the full amount less £10 admin fee, which is still a con, but I can accept £10, even £10 per person if they want to be greedy, but not to give me any of my money back in times like these is basically theft. They are not a reputable business in my eyes. There is no competition so they are able to charge ridiculously high prices for a tiny cabin and can then just choose to keep the money if something happens to you which means you can’t go. I’m very upset and angry with GWR and have made a complaint.

title: Awful Company
content: When travelling with GWR, when the ticket inspector checked my ticket, it transpired that my railcard had expired two days before. I had received no notification of this and was completely unaware of this. I apologised and said I would renew it on the spot, with the conductor watching. He said that it didn't work like that and I had to buy a new, full price ticket (despite having already purchased a ticket at 2/3 of the price). He refused to charge the difference and refused to get a manager that I could talk to about what had happened. He said I could appeal the decision after if I disagreed. I asked him to please allow me to renew the railcard, as that would make my ticket valid, and that I had very little money in this cost of living crisis. I was forced to buy a new ticket and when I went to appeal this, was told I could not appeal a new ticket and this was my fault. So I was forced to pay twice for the same journey with everyone I was interacting with being incredibly rude and unhelpful. In addition, the train was completely overcrowded (people sitting on the floor), and there was no refreshment trolley as a result (despite it being a boiling hot day). The train was also late. I was charged £100 for this journey (Totnes to London). I was absolutely disgusted and will not be travelling with them again.

title: I have spent an hour to put in a delay…
content: I have spent an hour to put in a delay repay claim. The GWR delay repay website says the website doesn't recognise my password. Which I know is correct. So I went through the process of resetting the password. It then said that the site was unable to reset my password. It seems pretty clear that GWR is creates barriers to people being able to put forward a delay repay claim. The delay repay site is extremely difficult and time consuming to navigate even when you can access it.Time consuming, cynical and frustrating.

title: First class is a scam here
content: Random noisy people sitting in first class. So if you pay extra for a quiet journey you’re in bad luck. Nobody comes to check tickets and to make sure only people with the right ticket sit in first class.

title: Overpriced
content: Missed my first train and was forced to pay double the original ticket just to get on the next one. Nearly tried to charge me quadruple the original too. Was told if I got a flexible ticket it would be fine; except the flexible ticket would have been hundreds of pounds more. Avoid GWR and get a coach instead.

title: Lost my ticket, it happens, but it will cost you
content: Lost my ticket, had proof of purchase in the form of seat booking and collection receipt, but wasn’t enough and first great western made me buy a new ticket before they would let me head home. One of the worst customer experiences I have ever had and the ones that are worse are for train travel in the uk as well. How they get away with it I have no idea?!? Money seems to be the beginning and the end for first great western! Customer experience seems to be way down the list of things that they give a f*#k about! It would be nice if they could make it an affordable and enjoyable experience! I would be far more likely to travel by train if it wasn’t to expensive and unpleasant.Th ask first great western for………. Nothing

title: Bad treatment of disabled customers
content: I had a very bad experience with GWR staff on the way to Bristol TM. The second I got on the train from Frome they asked if I had a ticket and then said you have committed an offence because i didn't have one. They made my say out loud why i didn't have one and I had personal reasons for not managing to get one in time which I didn't want to say, but I was always going to buy a ticket!! I told them how skint I am... they then made me say my home address out loud in front of a carriage of strangers who were staring at me, I said I don't want strangers knowing my address (as I've experienced harassment) but they were just like "oh..." and then still made me say it out loud. I have mental health and learning difficulties and this was really embarrassing as I get anxious enough being out in public anyway. Then when I got to the station I tried to tell one of the staff there that I wanted to make a complaint in person and she was like "there's not really anything we can do, I suppose you can talk to the station manager" She gestured at the station manager standing next to her, who then promptly walked off very quickly! way to receive feedback... I guess this is the only way to get you guys to listen to me now. Still can't afford the fine....

title: Excellent help and support from Bradley…
content: Excellent help and support from Bradley at gwr twitter. Thanks, Rory

title: Very little goodwill in the company!
content: I was issued a supposed goodwill payment of about £50 and went to claim it, to find out it had expired a couple of days before. The email issuing the link for the payment said nothing about a time limit to claim it. They refused to issue me another payment to replace the one not claimed.

title: Okehampton to Exeter
content: Today my sister and I travelled from Okehampton to Exeter and back.  The trains were on time and the staff were all smart, friendly, helpful and efficient. It was an excellent experience and we will now seek to use the trains more often. Thank you.

title: Amazing staff and efficient service
content: I went on a return trip from Taunton to London over Jubilee weekend. This was an extremely busy time and going there was completely smooth without a single problem. Coming back there were problems as lightning had taken out a signal (or something). This meant our train back to Taunton couldn't get to Paddington without major delays. They got everyone on an earlier train to pick up the delayed one at Reading and continue our journey without delaying anyone. They kept us all informed about everything continuously and everyone working within any of the stations knew exactly what was happening and could point everyone in the right direction. We were all apologised to several times even though we were all on schedule, thanks to all the quick thinking and hard work. We could not have been more impressed with the service while dealing with serious weather conditions. Thank you to everyone at GWR who made our entire journey stress-free.

title: A greedy company who leave paying…
content: A greedy company who leave paying customers to sit on the floor for their journey as they have oversold tickets.

title: Piled on like sardines
content: Other train services between Plymouth and London Paddington cancelledSignal failures leading to standstillsPoorly passengersNo fault of the driver bar agreeing to stop at all effected stations. I wish he’d said no so GWR could find a better solution to support all other cancelled services. Ownership to manage should not have been on one service. The 3:15pm service to London Paddington plays Martyre and overloads the train stopping at all stops that should have collected passengers on other cancelled services. It’s 18:33 and we are still on the train. It’s stuffy, smelly, noisy and overcrowded. Can’t breathe and no space to visit the loo. This was not a wise solution to the problem.

title: I put 1 star as I cannot put no stars…
content: I put 1 star as I cannot put no stars in my evaluation. I had reserved a seat and the train was over booked for the trip Lindon Paddington to Bristol. Also, the reserved indication above the seats was not working properly!Shameful! No wonder why railways in this country are at the verge of collapse. Not even a proper reservation they are not able to register properly in their systems.

title: Great Experience To + From Exeter
content: Fantastic clean, comfortable train..to and from Exeter from Clapham May 31st/June 2nd. Loos were even clean. Bang on time both ways. Diligent, helpful staff who kept passengers consistently advised what carriages to be in, where to alight etcMuch easier than driving, and with a cheap advance ticket overall a v good experience.

title: I used to be fine with Margaret…
content: I used to be fine with Margaret Thatcher. After all, I hate coal so her killing the coal industry was kinda a win in my books. Until I had to interact with Great Western Rail, and now I feel a strong desire to p*ss on her grave.

title: I could not get refund for my cancelled…
content: I could not get refund for my cancelled EMR trip. I did try to make a complaint but their website gives me an error "Please enter proper characters". I didn't use any special character just a plain text...

title: Now I remember why I don't get the…
content: Now I remember why I don't get the train much. Not only does it cost more than driving but it took so much longer. Our return trip to barnstaple from Exeter took 1hr and 50minutes, apparently there were delays due to bad weather, which was puzzling as it was only lightly raining and had only been raining for half an hour. Staff were nice though and the train was clean and not busy.

title: Will never travel via rail for any…
content: Will never travel via rail for any concert or event ever again. What kind of company sells  train tickets but doesn't provide enough trains. Disgusting!

title: Delay repay more like delay won't repay
content: I was travelling from Liskeard to Guildford via Reading yesterday. The journey to Reading ended up being delayed on route and diverted to Westbury where we were asked to switch to another train on an adjacent platform. The scheduled train was due to arrive in Reading just before 13.00. We eventually arrived at 14.10. By the time I arrived in Guildford I was an hour later than the original schedule. Applied for a refund via Delay Repay uploading the pdf copy of my ticket. Shortly after I received an email advising that my claim had been unsuccessful as 'the uploaded ticket was not valid for the journey undertaken'. What nonsense! The ticket had been checked by on-board ticket inspectors. I have appealed but don't hold out much hope. I suspect that I will have to pursue the matter via the Rail Ombudsman or Small Claims Court.

title: NOBODY RESPONDS TO INFORMATION GIVEN
content: Online claim for paid tickets for cancelled trains did not work. Have now been asked 3 times for information sent on 11 April.Have been told on different occasions that I would get a response after 3 to 4 days then 7 to 9 days then 28 days AND HERE WE ARE 45 DAYS LATER AND NO RESOLUTION.AND TODAY RECEIVED ANOTHER REQUEST FOR THE INFORMATION SENT ON 11 APRIL.THIS IS THE WORST CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE I HAVE EVER HAD.UPDATE….UPDATE…UPDATE 16 HOURS AFTER REVIEW REFUND APPEARS….SO SAD THE OPERATING SYSTEMS AND CULTURE AT GWR ARE NOT FIT FOR PURPOSE IN THEMSELVES.

title: Travelled from St Erth to Exeter St…
content: Travelled from St Erth to Exeter St David's - train seats are so hard and uncomfortable, toilet facilities are awful, water sprays everywhere when washing hands. They also need to look at putting a buffet car or shop in on these services, trolley service choice in pathetic.

title: I travelled from London Pad to Cardiff…
content: I travelled from London Pad to Cardiff Central.Honestly, after reading all the negative reviews here, I was scared to travel and was even considering taking the coach, but I risked it anyway. The trip was so worth it. The seats, the comfort, the staff, the views outside, everything was 10/10. Although, the tickets were kind of expensive, I would definitely use GWR trains to visit places in the near future.XNTN3B5X

title: Disappointing and more
content: I just don't get it. Some of the highest train prices in Europe but not the service to match. My 4 hour trip to London turned into six due to my train delayed at Exeter because there was not enough staff to run it on time. Non existent WiFi. How can you run a 4 hour evening train with only crisps, chocolate and mini cheddars as food. All cafes at all stations that I changed at were also closed. Shocking. Decent sized seats though.

title: The prices of tickets are ridiculous
content: The prices of tickets are ridiculous, I commute from London to Bristol and sometimes it’s 109£ for a single ticket, that’s more than going to Edinburgh or even Paris by train!!! So I end up taking the coach, which takes twice as long and it’s not eco-friendly. No wonder coaches are packed and trains empty. Oh and I love how on their website they say cheap tickets, cheap for who?!

title: Book with caution!
content: Bought a ticket with returns, and I was delayed for the morning travel (thanks TFL), so I purchased another but apparently according to GWR there was "no need" to do so. As a first time user they have denied me a refund for the error, and on top they take a £10 admin for processing refunds which is basically their way of saying "we'll give you a refund, but not all of it".A refund is a basic free service that no company should ever charge for. As you're returning what's rightfully belonging to someone else.

title: What a truly appalling company
content: What a truly appalling company. Bought a return ticket which had to cancel due to funeral arrangements and was then told that I had in fact bought a return 'journey' not a return 'ticket' for which a refund could not given only an e-voucher. I called up to question this and the customer service representative then tried to speak over me as I explained my situation and when I asked him to let me finish was told that I was being abusive and was raising my voice!!! This is my second poor experience in as many weeks so clearly something is not working in the GWR customer space! AVOID!

title: GWR have quick trains and are well priced
content: If I am honest I had a meeting in Swindon, travelled from Newport. 40 minutes.In a car an hour all day long and double the cost in a car.I was surprised how quick the train was, what 150mph, I am still stuck in the 80s slam door trains.On time, quick, cheaper than car.  A little lower perhaps from Newport to Heathrow and I'll travel on GWR everytime I go abroad. 1hr 42 into Paddington from Newport, sorry but that's quick.

title: Recent disappointing experience
content: Recent disappointing experience. Have held off using them as they are so expensive but got a good deal on split tickets. Was OK going out to Warminster, but coming back, a cancellation left me stranded for two hours and I had to take an alternative flight home. Due to the way I bought tickets, it was only a £8 refund. Would be hesitant to use again.

title: Terrible service
content: On 5.45 hour journey from Penzance to Paddington (journey time about the same as 100 years ago) stuck for 40+ minutes at Exeter as train manager joining at Exeter was 'stuck on another delayed train'. No catering during whole (what is turning into a 6.30 hour) journey due to 'staff shortage'. No water in toilet for whole 6.30 hour journey. Oh, and did I mention the pathetically inadequate wifi? And you're expected to pay a fortune for the privilege ...

title: Expensive
content: Expensive, uncomfortable journey. Very little to feel positive about.

title: Wifi didn’t work
content: Wifi didn’t work from Paddington to Newport on outbound or return leg week of 7/8 May 2022

title: Cancelled and overcrowded trains spoilt a nice weekend away
content: Usually drive but decided to try and be more environmentally conscious. Turns out to have been a big mistake. Gwr can’t even organise a short journey from Bristol to Gloucester without hours of delays and trains so full they resemble the tube at rush hour. Shocking service. 45 minute drive ended up taking three hours on the train. The vast minority of this trapped on the platform at Bristol with barely any seating. The journey cost about the same as driving and paying to park (even with using the two together railcard) If you want people out of cars you are going to have to do A LOT better.

title: Outrageous misogyny and discrimination from train manager aboard GWR Train
content: I am heavily pregnant at 8 months and had taken my son for a birthday (day trip) to London from Bath. As we all are aware, train prices are exceptionally high having been raised recently but as it was a birthday trip I had no problem paying the high return fairs, unfortunately I felt unwell during the day and with shooting pains was instructed by my midwife to return for a check up immediately. We caught the 4.32 Taunton train (an earlier train back to Bath)  it was relatively quiet) only to be accosted by the train manager ( who's shift was between Paddington and Swindon) He demanded we pay £50 extra to continue our journey and when I explained my situation he had absolutely no interest or regard. He could obviously see how pregnant I was and in considerable discomfort, He then threatened to eject myself and my son at the next station to wait for 5 hours on the platform for the right train. For someone in management for GWR This man* demonstrated an incredible amount of hostility, discrimination, chauvinism, lack of empathy and dismissive attitude  towards not only women but also pregnancy and health and safety. Being forced to pay £50 extra to travel two stops further with him threatening  to throw me off the train is a DISGUSTING abuse of power and quite frankly I will NEVER travel GWR again if this is their policy of grabbing cash over the safety and health of their passengers. BEWARE! seriously misogynistic senior management aboard GWR train services. This particular service went on to have significant delays on track stopping for over 30 minutes both at Swindon and just outside Bath which caused even more anxiety and distress both emotionally and physically. The next train manager ( a lady) was much more compassionate but asked me to lodge a formal complaint online ...I received an automated reply stating I wouldn't receive an official  response for 4 weeks!!!!! I am outraged and appalled at such blatant discrimination, greed  and lac of care from one of the largest rail networks in the country. The least I can expect is a personal apology and a refund but I highly doubt either of these will be on the cards.

title: Train cancelled from Paddington
content: Train cancelled from Paddington. Should  have been a ruined evening but no, quick run to Reading with time to buy  a snack before boarding the original train that was now starting from Reading. A 10 minute delay but with comfortable seat, a cup of tea and a snack it passed in no time. Well done GWR for overcoming a problem

title: Bike space not possible with advance ticket
content: When trying to book a bike space with an advance ticket for my journey, the website tells me I cant, because the service is full. If I select a standard ticket (3x the price) for the same service, the website is quite happy to book a bike space for me. What a pointless waste of time - travelling with a bike is difficult enough without this hassle.Ended up using the Avanti website as they don't suffer from this 'bug'

title: (GWR First Class Review)
content: (GWR First Class Review) A poor experience that is, in my view, worse than Standard Class. This review is based on a weekday service between Bristol Temple Meads and London Paddington.First, the comfort levels were poor. The seats were hard and uncomfortable and the coach far too bright. Second, as soon as the conductor had been through the carriage at the start of the journey, many standard class ticket holders simply relocated into First making the carriage loud and impossible to work. The conductor made no further checks.Third, the onboard catering was awful. Limited choice - far less than the standard class trolley service.In sum I won't use GWR First Class again as Srandard Class is broadly equal.

title: Good experience only
content: Thank you for connecting suburbs with big cities and providing a stable network. Personally I appreciated the chance to get to Southampton in 6 minutes using your services. Alternative transport had taken half an hour at double cost!Trains can not always arrive/depart in time, due to circumstances that occur, understandably. Overall: happy customer.

title: Late as usual
content: Train was okay for once, BUT DELAYED AS USUAL. 63% delays for me at Exeter st David's. Done the math. Always something  going wrong. Faffin, waiting in the cold, no refunds, no good excuse for being late again other than gwr messin things up. And the prices!? NATIONALISE TRAINS AGAIN

title: Absolute disgrace!
content: Absolute disgrace!I am simply fed up with GWR... this company should be a synonym for chaos, recklessness and no respect for work and customers. I am regular comuter between Tilehurst and London Paddington and I simply can not understand how this company operates. Delays, cancellations are happening every single day. It is a normality rather than exception. For them everything shorter than 15 minutes delay is absolutely daily routine. There are even more nasty tricks they're doing to their customers. They can change the platform within literary 1-2 minutes from the departure time very often leave you no time to walk between the beginning and end of the station. Did someone from GWR thought about disables and prams? I have used SWT trains and GWR service is not even close. Their timetable is all over the place. It looks like they do not now what to do if even slightest thing on rail go bad... GWR shareholders  please send your staff for training as now they are very incompetent employees (including managers as well).

title: Horrific abusive treatment by ticket inspector
content: My son (18) recently travelled back from Bodmin Parkway to Paddington to return to University from a family holiday in Cornwall.  He was travelling with an adult ticket +16-25 year railcard.  When the ticket inspector came round to inspect tickets, he could not locate his Railcard on his phone wallet as he had recently got a new phone. He called me for help (he is dyslexic and has mild ADHD) and I forwarded the receipt for the Railcard and the reference for the card.  I also sent him a copy of the railcard from my phone.  THe inspector would not take this from him and refused to talk to me on the phone.  My son was verbally abused by the inspector which was embarrassing in front of other passengers, who seemed horrified by this.  He threatened my son and made him pay £25 cash as he could not find the actual railcard.  He was told he could get this money back at Paddington.  The ticket inspector then exited the train at the next stop.  My son was really shaken by this but went to the Ticket office to get his £25 refund.  He was told he could not get a refund and was given a "Delay Repay" form which is the wrong form.  I have complained on multiple times to Great Western Railway (online as there is no phone number to contact them) and I have heard nothing.  I still have not received the refund for the excess he had to pay.  My son is living on student grant, and a full time student.  This is outrageous behaviour and there Great Western Railway have done nothing to act on the complaint or refund his money.  BE CAREFUL TRAVELLING ON GREAT WESTERN RAILWAY.  Inspectors apparently receive commission for all the excess payment they can get from travellers.

title: Useless, unreliable rabble pretending to run a train line. Avoid.
content: Let me start by sharing the link to 'Delay Repay'. Link not allowedIf you've had the misfortune of having to use GWR it's likely the most useful link anyone could give you. Please do claim. This rabble do not deserve to run a line as busy as this. In short, the level of delays from GWR is quite frankly a disgrace. Delayed trains are the norm; on time an exception all underpinned by friendly but poorly informed staff who will try, but invariably fail to help.Occasionally, despite best intentions, they may even hinder your journey by sending you on a travel merry go round that leaves you really stranded.Avoid GWR and the stations they run from if you can.May I suggest unicycling along the M4 as a safer, faster, cheaper and certainly more reliable way to get home.And do please do utilise delay repay every single time you're delayed.

title: Our Ukrainian family of 4 arrived last…
content: Our Ukrainian family of 4 arrived last night have taken the train all the way from Poland. The service, helpfulness and friendliness shown to them by the Paddington staff was fabulous. Thank you all for making them feel so welcome. 1830 from Paddington to cheltenham

title: GWR inflexible and a rip off
content: Okay so it's my mistake original tickets were ruined,I mistakenly put my wallet in the washing. So you would think GWR would replace even if they charged for this. I would have happy paid. But oh no, they couldn't replace once they were issued.  The resolution from GWR. Buy new tickets. Well I had to do that and for the same journey the cost had gone up to £165. Thanks for your no wonder people are not traveling by train

title: Daylight robbery
content: Shocking customer service GWR refused to refund me when I tested positive with covid, despite advising  them & cancelling in advance. title: Yet another delay and no information
content: Unbelievable farce trying to pick son up from St Germans from the 20.37/20.44 from London Friday night. One hour late, no info on station or via DM, excuses on train ranged from engine fault to missing crew. Why do things always fall apart on services once they pass Plymouth?

title: St Erth Station in Cornwall
content: Early train to Paddington and our ticket is not until 12.30ish.I managed to book earlier with the help of Sandra in St Erth Station. What a wonderful  to end a holiday with a helpful staff in the station. A credit to her.Thank you

title: Worse than useless.

title: Terrible - avoid if possible
content: Terrible, expensive service, staff couldn’t care less, delays on almost every train I’ve taken. Avoid rail travel with GWR if possible!!

title: First class but third class food
content: I travlled first class from Lonodn to Penzance (return - over 5 hours) and on both journeys there were no sandwiches available, just crisps and cake to eat.I complained to GWR: their response was pathetic - "We have recently made the difficult decision to stop serving sandwiches on board due to the reduced number of first class passengers" Why does the number of passengers matter? If I am the only first class passenger on a plane I will get first class food service, so what is wrong with GWR?

title: Poor Customer service
content: Pathethic customer service. On 6 April 2022, there was massive delay between slough to reading and reading to guildford. On normal day, it normally takes 1.5 hrs to travel slough to guildford but that day it took 4.5 hrs. Still delay claim department insist there was delay of 14 mins ????? GWR can u explain this ??? If so how on the earth I reached home in about 4.5 hrs instead of 1.5 hrs ????? 3 hours more than the usual time ....... title: GWR used to be ok, but now their behaviour towards customers borders on abusive
content: GWR used to be a decent train operating company, but since mid-2020 their conduct towards customers has seen a dramatic decline.  Most recently my wife and I used GWR to travel to Heathrow airport. We were greeted by a poster telling us to wear a face mask, even though this is no longer mandated by the UK government.  After buying our (rather expensive) tickets, the barrier attendant made the snide remark 'I don't know how you'll get all that luggage on the train' (we were within the luggage limits specified in the National Conditions of Carriage and GWR policy, travelling on a quiet and large train with ample luggage capacity).  We were then greeted by a poster advising us that simply staring at someone is now considered sexual harassment and perceived offenders would be reported to the police.  As I was moving our luggage along the corridor (no GWR staff had offered to help), another member of GWR staff decided to declare an item 'unattended' even though I was nearby and the luggage was within eyesight at all times.  He then became aggressive, lectured me that this was a major security hazard (this was at a provincial station not a major London terminus) and I wasn't allowed to bring so much luggage, though I knew full well I was under the conditions under which I had bought my ticket.   I said I was sorry for the disturbance caused and asked that he apologise too, reminding him that I was a customer - he declined and continued to be abusive.  Sadly this is not an isolated incident.  Earlier the same week, I witnessed a train manager spend twenty whole minutes giving a formal caution, to be followed-up in writing, to another customer simply because he had bought a ticket with disabled discount without a disabled rail card (this customer remained calm and co-operative throughout).  Furthermore, over the past two years, I (along with other customers) have frequently be threatened with fines and physical eviction from GWR trains by the British Transport Police if we fail to adhere to COVID regulations.  At times when these regulations were no longer mandated by the UK government, GWR staff accused those who didn't adhere to them of 'not respecting others.'  This has been accompanied by ubiquitous announcements, posters and platfom-mounted roundels promoting a COVID narrative that went well beyond anything sanctioned by official government policy and could be viewed as pschological abuse.  It's not the service I expect from a company I spend £1000s a year to travel with (usually with little or no luggage).  Cancelled, over-crowded and late trains I can accept; abusive behaviour towards customers I cannot.

title: The Mobile Gulag
content: I am a regular traveller between Bristol and Paddington. First the positives: by British standards, this is a reliable railway. I travel every week and generally my trains run to time and are rarely cancelled. Here endeth the positives. Standard class passengers on the new intercity express trains can look forward to levels of comfort comparable with a park bench placed underneath a light source brighter than the Sun. It’s clear that absolutely no attention has been paid to passenger ergonomics. The seats lack any thigh or lumbar support and are way too hard and upright. These same seats are used in commuter trains on the Continent and are not fit for intercity purposes. The arm rests are at the wrong height and anyway offer no comfort given they are made of a hard plastic over metal with no cushioning. As mentioned previosuly, the lighting is bright and ice cold. Combine all these factors together and even a sufferer of acute narcolepsy would struggle to rest, nevermind sleep in these moving torture chambers. There is no buffet car and the trolley service - if it appears (big if) - never has any sandwiches left. The staff make the best of the situation but there is no polishing to be done of these turds for trains that we are now lumbered with for the next 30 years. Whoever at the Department for Transport is responsible for procuring these mobile gulags should be made to spend the rest of their lives living in one.

Did anyone at First Group actually try sitting on one of these for 3 hours before they bought them? Compared to the seats on the West Coast Pendlino trains that Virgin Trains ran, that I would score as 8 out of 10, for comfort the GWR seats are 2 out of ten. Also the carpets are disgustingly filthy - they desperately need deep cleaning. Again on West Coast Virgin did that regularly. Now Avanti (First Group own part of Avanti) have taken over West Coast, no doubt standards will be dropping there too. The ticket cost an arm and a leg, far more than a comparable distance on West Coast. Why? To finish off, the lighting is a bright white LED. Come day or night it's on. Impossible to doze or sleep properly. Passengers have no control over it. Hopeless. Contrast GWR with West Coast - on West Coast each passenger has their own light so they can sit with it on or off. Much better. GWR are treating trains as if they are buses on rails. They are not. A train coach should have the same comfort as a road coach, not a double decker local bus. NEVER AGAIN. Just AWFUL.
