title: Well and truly annoyed at the service…
content: Well and truly annoyed at the service from Bristol Temple Mead to Exeter this evening. Arrived an hour before our train was due to leave. The amount of people trying to get on a teatime train with 3 carriages was crazy. We were the first on the platform and the only ones who couldn’t get on the train as people would not move along the carriages and the staff didn’t move them. This left 5 woman, one 6 months pregnant and a 75 year old stuck on the platform for more than an hour to wait for the next train, with no guarantee we would be able to get on that either.GWR charge so much for the train and should not be able to sell tickets if you cannot have a seat. Profiteering at its worse - money over the safety of their passengers.

title: Ryan Air of railways
content: +clean - first class basic. No good and service outbound to Exeter. Return offering was coffee, water and snack box(yoghurt, biscuit, pretzels).ADDED COMMENT 31/12/21Just received eventual response from GWR customer services after being asked to make contact as below. Response was ‘we sometimes tun out of refreshments, sorry’ - or should read don’t hold any stock. Woeful Customer service on every level.Don’t travel first class and save your money.  This is the ‘Ryan air of rail’

title: Travelling on 2140 from exeter to…
content: Travelling on 2140 from exeter to penzanceTrain “manager” rude and offensive- a lesson in manners would assist her in her managerial skills

title: Quite possibly the worst experience I…
content: Quite possibly the worst experience I have ever had! I booked online and made a mistake. Website I could make change at 10 pound per journey but could not be done online. I rang customer services, waited 15 mins to then speak to a rude, disinterested, unhelpful woman who said that there was nothing she could do. I had to book another ticket and apply for refund which will take 28 days. Coming up to christmas, Cardiff to Paddington return tickets are not cheap. I have to go to London for work but cant afford this. Lady not interested. I said I wanted to complain. She couldn't understand me so I had to use phonetic alphabet. If this was another industry such as financial services, the regulator would be all over it. Surely, they cannot get away with treating people so appallingly. As I havent been able to sort...guess what, as journey date is now closer, ticket prices has increased!

title: So happy to get my refund
content: About 3 weeks ago I had to cancel a journey on GWR as my son and one of his family who I was going to visit had Covid. I was quite upset about this and I had bought advance tickets so I thought that I would lose the money. However GWR policy until the end of the year is to provide e vouchers for future travel if you have to cancel an advance ticket - I got my voucher today and am so happy. Of course I will be travelling GWR a lot in the future to see son and grandchildren. Thanks - it means a lot!

title: Customer versus Process
content: Most weeks I commute once between Exeter St. David’s and Paddington.  06:48am from Exeter and 18:04 or 19:04 from Paddington.  As the 06:48 has been cancelled or delayed quite few times lately (“lack of train crew” or “delays”), including 10 minutes late this morning, which can happen, I thought surely they would be flexible to their customers (if possible) and allow me to travel back, one hour early back @ 18:04.  So I arrived at the train and asked the conductor if that was possible, as there clearly were quite few free seats (double green lights), her answer was flat no, but I “could buy full fare.” When I protested that it was being quite inflexible the response was “I don’t make the rules”. Surely some discretion and flexibility, where possible, can be adopted.  If the train had been full, I would have understood. This is where people should trump process.

title: Second world service all over the…
content: Second world service all over the "first class" expensive prices. Horrid uncomfortable seats. Barely ever a full food/drinks service, no action taken against rude or obnoxious or drunk or loud passengers, meh. Typical Britain.

title: No Refund on a Long Delay
content: A Halloween weekend trip up to Reading was awesome all except the travel...I had been delayed by several hours due to a crash so instead of getting home at around 5, I ended up getting home at 1am through generous lift donations. They note the delay repay request through the website yet mine was unsuccessful as I used "splitfare" so I paid for a train that I couldn't get on & cannot get a refund!Ridiculous!So many people, so little space yet cost so much money! I will not be using their services again.

title: Fabulous
content: Fabulous! This is the way to travel. Food and service was excellent.

title: Website almost deliberately impossible
content: I found the online booking process on mobile phone finicky. Kept jumping to time of travel I did not want. Having double checked everything committed payment. But email confirmation showed I was booked a week later than intending to travel. Then fun started trying to contact GWR to cancel, and realising too late to do that, to amend tickets. But they were both advance tickets which I learnt complicated things. Online amendment not suitable. Phoning hopeless, complaint process ridiculous (4 weeks later got answer to complaint saying cannot help as short staffed owing to covid (November 2021!). Read similar experiences from trust pilot with one review recommending Facebook page. Sent Messenger on gwr fb and within 5 minutes Jo replied with a link taking to a form for cancelling tickets which if submitted within 24 hours, amendment charge of £10 each way would not be charged. 4 weeks later refund was in my account. There was no way I would have found this link during time spent trawling gwr website. This review would have been zero stars if not for Jo.

title: Impossible to print out tickets at the…
content: Impossible to print out tickets at the station. Always sends me to the ticket office instead and I lose lots of time (and occasionally my train).The staff are nice otherwise.

title: Had a long three month wait for a refund And read the small writings before buying !
content: I did have big problems getting a refund However after a few emails and text I finally got a refund due to a couple of good team members thank you 🙏

title: Never take their train!!
content: Never take their train!!! Even when you don’t have choice. Took the train from swansea to London Paddington at 8pm and was stuck on train by reading middle of nowhere till 3am in the morning. I was meant to go Newcastle at 5am in the morning and didn’t have any sleep!! Nearly had a panic attack because the windows weren’t open and left my asthma pump at home!!

title: customer service via Twitter
content: I recently had cause to contact GWR via Twitter. Jess, the customer service rep, answered my question, sorted my seat reservation and answered my follow up questions. It was all very quick and efficient.

title: awful company!
content: awful company! expensive, and they never ask for feedback, as they know it'll be bad! i caught 2 trains on sat, bristol to london return, both were 10 carriages reduced to 5 so all the reservations were messed up.The return from London (last train 9.02pm!! its 2021!!!) was so full that pensioners and pregnant woman had to stand. It's worse than a 3rd world train service, and the prices are a rip off! Please remove the word 'great' from your company name. not impressed!!

title: Reading to Exeter and back this week
content: Reading to Exeter and back this week. For £20 each we upgraded to first class meaning we had plenty of room and about 30% of seats occupied both ways. Both trains were on time. We have trips planned to the Lakes and Cornwall. On both we will again check the cost of the upgrade.

title: Awful
content: Awful. i payed £60 online from bristol to newcastle and the ticket man on the train said i needed to pay £170 because my railcard was a month out of date. I take responsibility for not double checking my railcard but the fact its only recently run out is digraceful. And i wasnt even able to get a refund or money off the additional £170.

title: Exceptional customer service at GWR station Yeovil Penn Mill…
content: I was travelling via Yeovil Penn Mill (Maiden Newton to Paddington) where I needed to collect my tickets.  The ticket office staff Corrie and Jo were immediately friendly and obliging.  I had a very large suitcase with me and we briefly discussed my concerns about navigating the escalators on the London underground and Corrie suggested I enlist some help from one of the staff for my change of platform at Castle Cary which involved steps up and over the bridge.Having provided my tickets, a few moments later, Corrie came on to the platform to let me know there would be no staff at Castle Cary to assist me and offered a solution, to instead change at Westbury where the platform change was a mere few yards at the same level.  The arrival time at Paddington would be the same.  She printed new journey information for me and endorsed my tickets.  These two ladies seemed to work together exceptionally well, provided great customer service, had excellent knowledge of the stations, trains and staffing and are an absolute credit to Great Western Railway.  I am indebted to them for my hassle free journey, thank you.

title: DONT WAST YOUR TIME
content: Well absolute crock of crap get to Bristol Station no actual directions to were to go missed the train  staff are amazing told us not to reply on the app don't both buy a car or take a taxi

title: Was delayed by truck hitting the bridge…
content: Was delayed by truck hitting the bridge at Plymouth, got sent to Exeter to pay £70 Taxi which will be paid back from railway staff, was told to place it on the delay repay form. Sent off by post my ticket and Taxi Fare. Eventually got the ticket back, but didn't receive my £70. Spoke on the chat to which they say it goes through different department. Sent it off by email, never had a response, then told to send it via Online, which the website doesn't work funny enough as it is, they failed to refund me the money 2 months on. If you are reading this GWR, hope you are a shamed by your poor service, this has now gone through the Railway Ombudsman which I hope your name is gone. Could have made it easier for yourself, but decided as always to not listen and not bothered to do anything. Will be driving than using the train. Never ever use this company unless you have to. If this happens to you, keep a record evidence for what you pay.

title: Tbh every railway service in the uk
content: Tbh every railway service in the uk, but gwr is the one I have used the most over years.It is not hyperbole to say that I have not been on a long distance train that has arrived exactly on time in my life. Like ever. Gwr has stolen time from me and their fairs are extortionate.

title: Bad Manners By GWT
content: GWT have just cancelled my train today, so completely messing up my arrangements.  No proper apology which is what really irritates me.  Just to say "Unfortunately" your train has been cancelled you can take the next one, doesn't cut it.The GWT client services should get a grip and learn how to do a proper apology.  Learn some manners.

title: Would give zero stars if I could tbh
content: Would give zero stars if I could, I’ve literally had to take on a second job to afford my train tickets to my job in London and even then can’t actually remember the last time I could find a seat on the train. Lucky if they’re only five minutes late but more often than not they’re unacceptably late or cancelled. Most unreliable and worst value for money around. Cheers lads!

title: GWR trains saved my life
content: GWR trains saved my life. Simple as that. They provided the service as promised and got me home. The train was on time and very comfortable. GWR are life savers - unlike Stagecoach buses and the local taxi companies that left me to die. GWR are heroes!

title: Extremely helpful
content: I have recently contacted GWR via Twitter, regarding merchandise and have nothing but praise for the way my query was handled. The responses were swift, pertinent and the staff involved, Brad and Michaela, were extremely helpful.GWR is my local train provider and the last journey I undertook was as smooth and unproblematic as usual. I use trains as much as I can and it is certainly my preferred mode of travel. Thank you, GWR.

title: I needed to change my seat bookings and…
content: I needed to change my seat bookings and contacted GWR via Facebook.  Thank you to Brad whose customer care was exceptional - all sorted out.  Recommended!

title: Great refreshments
content: There’s a great selection of refreshments on offer in 1st class: peanuts, biscuits, fruit cake, crisps and now flapjack.  It has been updated since the summer to include deliciously tasting flapjacks. The seats are comfy and the decor’s nice too.

title: Have someone manning the phones please...
content: They need to get more people in their call centre. I've phoned three times this week and waited for between 20-45 minutes each time before giving up. They warn you may be waiting "up to 15 minutes" which is presumably a bad joke.

title: Terrible customer service
content: I never usually do this, but I literally took it upon myself to go on the web and write a review. GWR customer service division needs total revamping. A bunch of unresponsive and slow representatives. My trip was delayed by 3 whole hours, to and fro. I requested a refund, they refused me one and their reason was "Used Ticket". What does that even mean??? I kept calling their customer service to demand an explanation and I waited a whole 1 HOUR with no response.

title: The worst reply’s
content: This was on gwrs Twitter and I was train spotting at Bridgwater and saw a HST and got a 2 tone and then after got barked at by other train spotter who where there and gwrs responded with this “good morning Thomas, toot toot! Excellent video of our HST Castle class leaving Bridgwater railway station- Ben”

title: Constant delays
content: Constant delays. The driver's seem too embarrassed to give reasons as to why trains are running into London an average of 10 to 20 minutes late every F morning. Total BS service.

title: A real pain if you travel with a bike.
content: A real pain if you travel with a bike.GWR trains are nice and run as on time as any in the South West. But, I hate the fact you have to reserve a space for your bike every time you travel. They are one of the very few operators that mandate this... and it's so much bureaucracy. It's also really annoying when you don't know exactly what train you are going to want to get when coming back from an event. Wish they were like most operators where it's just first come first served.

title: Why pay when you can get a free ride
content: I can understand why people complain about train fairs. Caught train with my wife on Sunday. Seats reserved or so we thought. Was told to f*** off a number of times by what appeared to be a drunk passenger. As the computer system wasn't working moved to 2 vacant seats which we vacated when it's occupiers arrived. Later on into the journey conductor arrived only to find drunk passenger had no ticket and too was abused by him. Was told to get off at next stop....surprisingly didn't. Conductor didn't return and we heard him laugh as we pulled off and laughed an hr later when we arrived into London. There was also 2 other passengers who decided to get on this train early (never paid the extra and never got off) preventing a family of 4 sitting together around the table they too reserved. Don't blame the conductor as can't deal with someone like this on his ownDisgraceful....I feel for the people who continuously pay good money for this poor service!!!!

title: Really excellent customer service.
content: Really excellent customer service.Saturday 2.29pm train to Cheltenham from Paddington, the staff I encountered were so professional and helpful and attentive and this was not just me. They were patient explaining things to other passengers too. Train was clean, modern and comfortable. This is how train travel should be and unfortunately in the UK, often as not it isn’t, but please GWR keep this up, as I am not often this impressed to actually write a review!

title: I would like to thank GWR for an…
content: I would like to thank GWR for an excellent customer service. I took my parents who both have mobility problems to their train at Gloucester last Monday morning. I was worried about how they would manage to get a heavy case onto the train.I didnt have to ask, the train attendant spotted they made need help, unfortunately I didn't get his name, but he was so helpful. He even rang Weymouth to make sure they had help when they arrived. They were met and helped to a waiting taxi.Excellent customer service from the staff at Gloucester Train Station. And of course Weymouth!

title: Updated: negative experience fixed with help from Michaela
content: Train was apparently 58 minutes late, so I was not entitled to the full compensation as it was not 60 minutes. We were told on the day we would receive full compensation. They take abreally long time to respond to emails and Facebook messages. The train stopped without clear communication on the tracks and at another station. We couldn't sit next to each other despite our tickets as we needed to switch trains due to the issue that caused the delay. To not get the full compensation because we were 2 minutes short despite these conditions is hugely insulting. A member of staff I spoke to on Facebook was blunt and she did not listen to my query properly, confusing it with something else. Edit: after some time GWR did contact me below and were eager to get this sorted for me, which I really appreciate. Michaela was able to secure a good resolution and I have changed the rating accordingly. Thank you for your help.

title: Split & Save is RUBBISH.
content: Literally the worst company I've ever had the misfortune of using. I bought an open return ticket, to which they 'split and saved' me money on (sounded great!). Only to go and use it and it's gone? Oh, because they bought me a ticket that went out of date before the month period was up and booked me another 'super off peak', which means I can only travel after 7pm till 5am, but the only train they offer after this time is 10:30pm, getting in at 05:37 into London ....hmmm a single young female travelling on an overnight train for 7 hrs, with a full-time job to go straight too.... sounds ideal, not. The phone service is no help either, they are a 'third-party' so can't do anything remotely helpful. Brilliant. So, I'm having to travel during my work day tomorrow because SUPER off peak means I can only travel after 10am till 4pm. I didn't even book this, THEY changed my ticket and sold it to me as a better price?! I am NOT happy.

title: Simply the worst
content: Simply the worst. Were very rude to my disabled friend have escalated

title: Really great quick efficient service…
content: Really great quick efficient service from GWR (specifically Jess) Using WhatsApp meant my question was answered far quicker than sitting in a telephone queue! Would highly recommend and use again

title: Where do I even start?
content: Stupidly overpriced tickets, hit and miss service and rude staff at stations.Your amazing ticket machines weren't working on the day before my trip (at 6:57am!) so I took a picture of your sign on said machines which said to use the reference number in the meantime.Your rude, unempathetic staff didn't care at all and made me run to get a ticket from the machines which were now working. There is NO logical reason at all to not open the stupid gates AT ONCE since they are always open shortly before that time. Your people are simply @ssholes, that's it.I've had enough of your lousiness and expensive gold-plated tickets.Buzz off GWR!PS: Drive yourself to work and you won't have to put up with any of this.

title: No tickets sent & had to pay for same journey twice
content: When purchasing my train journey, I opted for tickets to be posted by 1st class mail. Never again.I was advised that if my tickets do not arrive 24 hours before departure to call GWR who will arrange for the tickets to be collected at the station. After 50 minutes of being on hold, I told Great Western Railway that they didn't arrive. GWR Fill in a form whilst I am on the phone and say that everything has been arranged for my ticket collection.Got to the station and the desk know nothing about the collection and I have to pay for a new ticket in order to travel.I call GWR once again to explain the situation. I was told that a manager will call me back in 24 hours to resolve my case. I am also given a case ID to reference the issue. I have received no call back and now I am back on hold to Great Western Railway.Absolutely shocking customer service. I will never buy train tickets from GWR again and will advise anyone to shop elsewhere.

title: Ticket Issue Resolved!! Thanks Sam!
content: At my local station I couldn't collect my tickets and staff were beyond useless, giving me a handwritten note to allow me to travel!!! Didn't even put my destination on it, attempting to travel from London to Bristol and return a week later! I was so upset and managed to blag my way to London Paddington where Sam at the GWR Ticket Office actually understood what the issue was and fixed it, managing to print me tickets to make my journeys so much easier. Unfortunately I can't find anywhere on their website to say thank you to Sam, I did thank Sam at the time, before running for my train, but everyone at GWR should also know how great he was.(Paddington 3087 on 11.10.2021 @10.56)

title: Indifference to passenger safety.
content: Bristol Parkway Staff displayed an appalling disregard, indifference and arrogance to my criticism of their Safety Procedures on their premises.  I took it on myself to verbally warn the perpetrator that I feared an accident was possible but he was unconcerned and hostile, even attempting to prevent my complaint.  I reported this to the Station Supervisor who refused to identify himself and stonewalled my request for action and a method of reporting the situation as I was seeing it.  Within fifteen minutes of my conversation an accident occurred as I predicted, fortunately this was property damage only and no persons were hurt.I have called the GWR Customer ‘Helpline’ and written a Complaint using their on-line system but received no reply other than the generic “We are experiencing high call volume during Covid” and “It will take up to four weeks to reply to your message”.My later telephone conversation with the Parkway Manager merely confirmed that I am in no position to criticise their arrogance and that he would take action against me!

title: GWR died the moment they took away the…
content: GWR died the moment they took away the HST Inter City Experience, Buffet Carriage,Fully stocked Bar, with ice cold Beers Wines and Ciders, Bacon Rolls, cakes everything to travel on a 5 HR Service to Penzance from Paddington , Comfy seats, Plush Beautiful leather seats in First Class, curtains, Tinted windows, AC that can be controlled on the Train not at the Depot, It is a total Joke now, But Hey GWR don't care ANYMORE , so Sad.

title: Who on earth decided that the seats on…
content: Who on earth decided that the seats on these trains were acceptably comfortable? It’s physically painful sitting on them for more than about 20 minutes. Absolutely laughably bad decision.

title: Very good service. No major complaints (so far).
content: I've never had any problems with the website or the app (except a few bugs here and there on their app). Also, they have been very good at giving money back for any delays and cancellations.However, I haven't used their services since Covid hit so I'm not sure if there have been any major changes since.Deducted a star because trains on the app are no longer labelled as peak, off peak and super off peak. Also, train seat reservations are useless because they are never working on the train/ people don't ever seem to follow them.

title: Can't take a screenshot of my eticket…
content: Can't take a screenshot of my eticket to claim delayrepay, when I try it won't let me 'for security reasons'. My train was two and a half hours late arriving at my destination. Tried multiple ways to send proof of ticket purchase with my delay repay application form. Ticket number is not visible on etickets which you need to submit a claim. Eventually found a way to send what I hoped was proof of purchase and received a response today telling me my claim was unsuccessful. I'm furious. My delayrepay refund that gwr assessed is 70.60, not an unremarkable amount. Do not know where to turn next. Will never purchase etickets again, will stick to paper tickets, as I have made delayrepay claims before with paper tickets and it is a straightforward, easy process.  If anyone can help me I'm open to ideas to resolve this problem!

title: Delay Repay
content: Delay Repay. My train was one hour late arriving at final destination.So I claimed on Delay Repay.GWR 2341 351 981 was unsuccessful due to not all the tickets being uploaded. Not true they were all uploaded.So I appealed GWR 2491 352 923. Now they say ticket number not visible. Not true the ticket number is clearly visible.They obviously have no intention of compensating even though one hour late does qualify for compensation!

title: I made an error in my booking...
content: I made an error in my booking and in my panic I messed up my refund form. Contacted GWR through Facebook to see if they could help and sure enough my request to cancel the refund(in order to complete the process correctly the second time around) was promptly approved by Celia. Very happy with the polite service and help I received.

title: A superb Pullman Dining experience!
content: Just got home after a trip down from London on the 1848 London to Swansea service on 27th Sept. From the second we turned up at the dining car to the minute we arrived home, the whole experience was superb. The crew greeted me by name when we arrived at the door to the dining car, showed us to our table and got us settled. There was no rush to take our orders, nothing was too much trouble and we were made to feel so welcome. Even though it is a limited menu, the food was fabulous. I had smoked trout to start, cod loin and plum tart for dessert. We jokingly mentioned that we enjoyed custard and they certainly obliged! The starter and main course were gorgeous and the dessert really was the metaphorical "icing on the cake". The chef even gave us an extra jug of custard to ensure we did not go hungry. Julie, Diane and Kay, you were superb. Absolutely superb! Chef was not bad either!  The "Custard Boys" went home happy and We Will Be Back! Thank you so much for making our trip so enjoyable, a real Dining Club atmosphere.

title: I booked return tickets with reserved…
content: I booked return tickets with reserved seats.  On both trains the seats I had reserved were showing as available.  Not a problem as I was getting on a the beginning of each journey but if I had been getting on part way through I would have been standing.

title: Avoid. Management clearly have no clue how to run a transportation service.
content: They'll cancel most of the trains 20 mins before they're scheduled to leave. No service improvement in years, management clearly have no clue how to operationalise a transport business. Children could do a better job. Utterly useless.

title: Good trip
content: Travelled from London to St Ives first class.Train was punctual and clean. Seats not as comfortable as some but adequate once I'd mastered the recline, good width and legroom for a big woman.Very attentive and polite staff who were unfailingly polite and helpful dealing with a elderly and rather demanding passenger sitting near to me. Four drink and snack trolley visits. Overall first class not as good as some other intercity rail companies but not bad.

title: No customer service
content: No customer service, been on hold for over an hour. Been promised a refund for a train that was over 12 hours delayed - but they will not send it to my bank account. Get a bus.

title: No reply to my tweet giving false…
content: No reply to my tweet giving false information on their app could of cost me £60 when their useless app stated to go through London however my ticket doesn’t allow that 4 hours ago I sent them a message no reply useless incompetent TOC

title: Just-avoid gwr
content: Just bad on every level

title: Ticketing IT is hopeless.
content: A few days ago I tried to buy a return ticket via GWR's ticketing website from Bath Spa to London Paddington, which came up 'Ticket Unavailable'.After retrying, and failing - and having had problems before - I went to thetrainline.com and bought the tickets I needed there and then.GWR IT just not fit for purpose.Bad customer service, or more accurately, no service.

title: Lounge facilities at Penzance Station
content: We travelled with two friends on the overnight sleeper from Paddington to Penzance on 9 September. An excellent journey with very helpful and cheerful carriage staff.We were particularly pleased to be able to spend time in the lounge at Penzance station as we waited for transport which was transferring us to Lands End airport. The steward on duty was very welcoming and informative. She was an impressive an impressive ambassador for the Company. The facilities were excellent: comfortable seating, tea and coffee, light snacks and TV all contributed to a very pleasant experience after a long journey.

title: Truly the worst of the worst
content: Website is impossible to use, insisting on; booking a seat - then won't let you, making an account - then won't let you, selecting e-ticket - then won't let youGWR is going under in 2023/24 - you heard it here first

title: Great customer service
content: Both Brad and Celia were incredibly helpful regarding my GWR booking. I can't praise them enough. Thank you.

title: Brilliant experience brad was…
content: Brilliant experience brad was incredibly helpful!

title: Cancel too many trains at weekends…
content: Twice I have had cycle reservations in the last three weeks on trains to London, then within 3 hours of leaving the train is cancelled, I can't get a cycle reservation on the next train so can't travel.

title: Abusive fares and unreliable services
content: Reading to London must be the most abusive fare on the planet. Further more there aways are disruptions and delays.

title: No response from GWR - Totally unacceptable and terrible…
content: Totally unacceptable and terrible customer service. My online query was never answered. At least compensate us for your shocking lack of care for your customers.

title: Unimpressed with GWR.
content: GWR are usually very good but they seem to have a problem with their seat booking. After booking return tickets from Liskeard to Gloucester I noticed I had no reserved ticket for return leg Bristol Temple Meads to Liskeard on 11 th Sept .After numerous phone calls eventually a customer representative informed me via Twitter that ' nobody can reserve a seat on this train. This is totally contrary to previous information stating ..You must have  a seat reservation to travel !!! So frustrating to have wasted so much time trying to reserve a seat on this service. You can do better than this GWR.

title: Tried to make reservations from…
content: Tried to make reservations from Guildford to Oxford to Worcester to Guildford.  Website insists you reserve seats and then tells you you can’t.  No e-tickets, they have to be collected from a station.  Insists you open an account, and then won’t let you.  Given up, I’ll drive.

title: Salisbury to Southampton GWR "services"
content: Salisbury to Southampton service around 1230 on Sat 4th Sept. Service was overly full (3 carriages only). Only one window open making for a very hot and uncomfortable journey. No Guard to be seen or heard on this service.Are GWR aware that there is a pandemic ?Returning on the 1710 from Southampton, there were no toilet facilities working on any part of the train and reportedly not to be fixed before the train arrived in Bristol. There was a Guard who offered to oblige customers with comfort stops at stations along the way. "Please sir, I need a wee".Nothing like C21st travel on GWR trains!Members of the GWR Board should try travelling on trains like these. Might it be pointed out that the service is for human beings and not for cattle. Noting, of course, that many services offered by GWR, at least those seen to be passing through Salisbury, would not qualify to carry cattle, as assessed against Health and Safety standards for livestock - too hot, too crowded and inadequately ventilated.For many people, this service is a necessity in getting to Bristol, Cardiff, Southampton,  etc., perhaps to access the hospitals. They do not have the option to travel by other means, or to pay less elsewhere.How about providing them with a service that is consistently fit for purpose ?Is this so much to ask for the ever-increasing cost ?!

title: The worst experience ever
content: The worst experience ever. It's the hottest I've ever felt in my live. There's no windows to open, no vents to blow out cold air. Literally the worst 45 minutes ever. I was so close to getting off early and catching a taxi the rest of the wat, I've neve had so much sweart pour out of me. Never again will I catch one or you trains.

title: Never trust this railway
content: Never trust this railway, the only thing you can guarantee about them is they will find a way of fining you no matter what ticket you purchase. I have travelled on railways all over the uk but never have I found a railways so incompetent.You can buy anytime returns which are not valid anytime, you can buy tickets for specific trains which are not valid on the named train. They bring a whole new level to criminal travel companies.Absolute disgrace

title: Theale Station staff are fab
content: (OK, I'm putting aside all the other issues I have about travelling on the rail network.)I wanted to thank your ticket staff working on Monday at Theale station. title: We had seats reserved on the train from…
content: We had seats reserved on the train from Bodmin to Reading. When we got to the station we found our carriage didn't exist. They had taken off several carriages. So staff very helpfully found us a seat to sit together. The toilet hadn't been cleaned. Urine on the floor plus abandoned clothing. Put soap on my hands only to find no water to rinse them. Tried to get on the website to complain and found I had to answer so many questions and upload my eticket onto the email. I couldn't do it so wasn't able to complain. You see, l don't actually believe they cancelled all those carriages because of staff shortages as there were plenty of stewards on the train. I believe it's because they couldn't fill the train so it was a cost cutting exercise. Not so many customers since covid and that's why they are advertising. Problem is they don't tell you GWR is not so great! And not hygienic. Go by car or bus!

title: GWR is usually a reliable service with…
content: GWR is usually a reliable service with polite and friendly staff. I also like the recycling services at key stations. Usually I’d give them 4 stars. However, engineering work got delayed so all services on the Bristol Temple Meads line to Severn Beach and back got cancelled today. I know COVID rates have meant people have been off work recently, but GWR failed to provide replacement buses from the station. I work at Severn Beach and there is no direct bus service there from where I live. I would have had to take a two or three buses and ended up spending £25 on a taxi to work! I hope GWR provide replacement buses from stations in the future… Thank you. Tim Woodward.

title: Absolutely useless
content: On 5 July I bought an advanced first class ticket on line from London to Plymouth. I paid extra for the ticket to be posted to me as I did want the hassle of picking it up from the station. By 14 July it had not arrived. I telephoned their customer services and waited 20 minutes for the phone to be answered. After a discussion I was told that due to Covid19 Royal Mail was delayed. However I said this was rubbish as a few days earlier I had ordered some euros which had been delivered promptly. I was advised to go onto the website, ask for a refund and buy another ticket. I did so but was unable to get a refund because advanced tickets cannot be refunded! I therefore telephoned again this time waiting 30 minutes for the phone to be answered. I was told how to use the help to claim on the website. I decided to wait two more days in case the ticket arrived. It didn’t so went online to book a new ticket. To my horror the price had increased by £83. Obviously I did not purchase one but telephoned again saying that no one had told me that the price would increase. My only option now I am told is to telephone the day before I am due to travel (and no doubt wait ages for the phone to be answered) to tell them my ticket has not arrived. I am told that it will then be a “manager to manager” agreement that I can pick the ticket up from the station; something I did not want to do in the first place!Incidentally I have made a formal complaint on line and have heard nothing, not even an acknowledgment. Why could they not have posted another ticket? Why couldn’t they have emailed me a ticket?I will never book with them again!

title: Absolutely appalling service
content: Absolutely appalling service. Trains constantly incredibly late and often cancelled without warning. Ticket prices are ridiculous, it's actually cheaper and quicker to drive the vast majority of the time (and yes, that includes both petrol and parking).

title: Worst App I have ever used
content: This is the worst App I have ever used. And the idea that the planned future is to phase out the Train Line app and impose the GWR app on everyone for online train bookings is beyond surreal. It is a nightmare. It constantly requires you to change your password time after time after time and even then fails to give you access to the one thing you want - your ticket if you have booked with them. As to changing your ticket - first you have to buy a new ticket ( and when you get to payment it stops working time after time) Then you try to cancel the old one. Time after time it fails. Then you call GWR and after 40 mins they say they can’t help you over the phone but you should go to the station. Except that NO train station will help you change a GWR ticket bought on line even though the ticket office is operated by GWR. Thanks to a wonderful man  whose identity I shall protect I managed to get a refund and compensationBut I shall never ever use this App again until GWR realises that in 2021 the only thing that matters  to a consumer trying to book on line is that its App is fit for purpose.

title: Absolutely hopeless
content: Absolutely hopeless, I will never be booking with them again!I have been trying to book train tickets to Cornwall in August for about a month now. Everytime I went to reserve a seat and pay, it would tell me there was an issue (though wouldn't tell me what that issue was) and it couldn't process the booking. After doing some research it seems you can't book more than 6 weeks in advance at the moment until timetables are confirmed. A little annoying but fine, I waited. Went to buy the tickets this morning and it finally let me reserve my seats, so I went through to the payment, confirmed through my banking app, and the GWR website said booking failed. Tried it again, and the same thing happened. Checked my bank statement and I have been charged TWICE and don't have a booking to show for it. I try to call their customer line, twice, and both times was waiting for an hour with nobody answering the phone. Tried to message on Facebook and Whatsapp as they otherwise recommend, and I did get a response here, though very unsympathetic saying I had to wait for the bank to refund me.To add to the context here, each attempted booking was £250, so this is £500 I am missing at the moment, with no idea when it will be returned to me. All because they have a terrible website that doesn't work and an unresponsive support team.I then this afternoon get a response to a case I made 4 weeks ago asking why I couldn't book the train back then, and it says if I have any questions to email back, and to expect a response in 20 days. Laughable.They are obviously understaffed, perhaps from making redundancies due to COVID. Obviously they don't understand that maintaining good customer service will keep people using your service, therefore this is not a department that you can afford to make cuts in.Booked in the end with Trainline and as always they are great and reliable so I have my tickets. Though am still £500 down.

title: Shocking customer service
content: Avoid (if possible) They charge a £10 admin fee to refund tickets bought on the GWR app.) I bought tickets on the app last Sunday (since their ticket offices are closed most of the time after work these days!) and did not use them as I fell ill. Tried to get a refund or to change the day of travel on the day of travel however as the tickets cost less than £10 and GWR charge a £10 admin fee (for what? Processing a refund? title: Think twice if your going on holiday.
content: My partner pre booked a train ticket as advised with covid, from Newbury to Cornwall. Due to being hard working and self employed, he was joining myself and our children a day later, so he wouldn't let a client down.He wanted to dive down in his work van, but i convinced him to catch a train down after work and have a rest after a long day working. Also we could then travel home as a family which includes our disabled son, so making life a little easier. A few days before he got a message saying his train was cancelled, so he managed to change his ticket to a train which was running a few minutes later? Pretty much the same train! To be able to do this he had to pay an extra £15 and couldn't get an allocate seat like he previously had! Seems like you just wanted to squeeze some more money out of him!On the day of his travel, he left his van at work and got his very nice client to drop him off at newbury station to start his journey. On his way to reading station he was then informed the train he was catching next to Cornwall had be cancelled!!!!! So he was stuck at reading, and left stranded!!! We live in Benson, his work van was in newbury and his family in Cornwall. So as there were no more trains that would get him to Cornwall that day, and even if there were he'd have to pay for another ticket as the people at reading said his ticket was non refundable and he'd have to contact gwr (which he tried, but waited 15mins trying to speak to someone on the phone before giving up). So all he could do was PAY for another ticket to get him back to Newbury, where he started. And get a taxi back to his van and then drive all the way to Cornwall, in order not to disappoint our children. After a long day at work and wasting his time starting his train journey, which now seems that you really had no intention of running in the 1st place. Seems you like to take as much of peoples money as you can under false pretenses.This was our 1st time putting our trust in rail to do a long distance journey. After this massive let down and lack of any sort of decent customer service, we certainly wont be using rail again. We will stick to the roads! In total he brought his original ticket for £79.80.Then had to pay £14.20 to transfer his ticket to a train running a minute earlier than the original. Then £7.10 to get a train back to Newbury station after starting his journey. THEN HE HAD TO FILL HIS VAN UP WITH PETROL TO GET TO CORNWALL AFTER YOU LET US DOWN TERRIBLY.

title: Customers not treated equally
content: A vehicle hit a bridge, ahich I understand is not GWR's fault. They had to run safety checks. This delayed trains. But the London trains managed to make it on time. They always do. But the Gloucester train, which I was catching, was late. The train was 45 minutes late. Apparently, delays of up to 15 minutes were expected. Well, my train was 3× the expected wait. I understand the incident with the bridge is not GWR's fault, but I do not believe we are treated equally. The big London trains always have ample coaches and the trains I catch never have more than 3 coaches. We are crowded and standing up. It's impossible to maintain social distancing. And why, if any train is going to be delayed or cancelled, is it always the little Gloucester or Worcester trains?What I am saying is that it doesn't matter if you are first class, going to London or Filton Abbey Wood, we are all customers  and deserve to be treated equally. This is a serious issue that needs to be addressed.

title: Paying extra for first class isn’t worth it
content: Paid the extra for first class and the seating was very comfortable and lots of space. However the trolley came through around every 1.5 hours and I only found out that they didn’t have any food outside of the biscuits available other than crisps - which I had to pay for. My train was also delayed by 23 mins and my connecting train at St Erth to St Ives didn’t wait just 2 mins to make that connection. So now I’m really late and haven’t been able to get food on my 5 hour journey. I get that it’s COVID but lack of communication really made it a bad experience. Very disappointed.

title: Appalling! Not the Trains! The Staff!
content: Appalling Service from Staff. I was in First Class and this staff member walked in, asked if I could read (A sign that was on a slide door that slid open as you approached it therefore wiping out any chance of you actually reading it!) and told me to pack up my things and get next door. He forcefully made sure I went, pushing me as I was 'Too slow' packing up my things, even though I am disabled with only the use of one arm and epileptic. When I explained this, he told me that me being in the wrong carriage was nothing to do with me being disabled, and I didn't look disabled in any case!He tried to get me into the next carriage but the refreshment trolley was coming the other way. I was trapped, couldn't move. title: “I am now that guy”.....
content: I have used GWR services on my journeys back and fore work for around 15 years or more, early mornings and early evenings. Always friendly and reliable staff.Come 12/04/21 after countless journeys where everything is checked (keys, phone, wallet (the usual) then exit, on this day however I have now become that man - I left my “Apple Watch ON CHARGE on the seat. Not just any watch, “a 40th birthday present from my daughter!!!!!”First things first - I panic.... worry.... stress etc etc. I then do what all men do - say nothing and hope no one will notice! Then brain wave - google GWR lost property, click a link, add my details then sit back and try and not bring up “I left my watch on a train” into any conversation!I then find GWR on Twitter - I start my message with “Hi - this might be a long shot....” give the details. I’ve noticed it’s now getting quite late in the evening so wasn’t expecting any reply until the morning after, if at all.Low and behold, minutes later,...... I confess etc etc, Mrs cursing, daughter shouting, scenes! A message comes through in all the distraction, so I go through my predicament about now being “that guy.”They promise to try and get hold of someone and get back to me ASAP. A little time came and went but unfortunately nothing in the evening. Obviously during today I’m randomly checking to see if I’ve had any DM’s.This afternoon I had a message from Celia via Twitter, who had also taken my message the previous evening on behalf of GWR Team “confirming” my watch had been found safe and will be held for me to come and collect at my convenience.Excellent news, Mrs happy, daughter jubilant, scenes! The service I had throughout my “ordeal” has been excellent. All staff that I spoke to directly or indirectly via Twitter certainly went the extra mile for me to help and I couldn’t be more greatful!So use the GWR lost property link - easy,Then always worth sending a message like my long shot.Happy days.Thank you GWR!

However, on booking a short trip to London last November 2020, and experiencing usual difficulties online, I picked up the phone in great trepidation. I was able to book a return journey without too much difficulty. Of course, HM Government then imposed a London lockdown so travelling on my dates was not permitted. I went online and found an option to apply for a replacement travel voucher: voucher because of the nature of tickets I'd booked but that was no problem for me. There then ensued about two months of the much anticipated GWR chaos, my application rejected, not valid tickets, cursory examination of my complaints, quickly dismiss with one line emails: much more like the GWR I'm accustomed to. I picked up the phone again. Another stroke of luck. Another GWR employee actually wanting to help me. After nearly three months, my issue was resolved within a couple of days. GWR has a long long way to go before I'm convinced it's much more than the awful company I'm used to dealing with. But there are glimmers of hope. Well deserved three stars.

title: Refusing to modernise
content: So somebody is abroad and is travelling to the UK and wants to buy a ticket with this lot. For delivery they give you the option to either post it to a UK address or pick it up from a machine/ticket office at the station. Great. So now you pay by Paypal and because you're not in the UK you can't have it delivered at your UK address so you choose the station pickup option. Excellent. Now we are in the coronavirus pandemic and things change from one day to the next so it turns out you can't come into the UK on the selected date. So now you're looking to change that ticket to a different date. Now the only option to have it delivered is via a UK address which creates a conundrum only they know how you can solve. So you have a relative who can receive the ticket to their UK address and then post it to you so you pick that option. But they don't send you the full amended ticket, they send you an excess ticket which is not valid unless you have the original ticket. Nobody is going to tell you that you have to pick up the original ticket from the machine to use the excess ticket. And if you used Paypal as the method to pay then you cannot pick it up from a machine because there is no provision for that, you have to go to the ticket office and get it from there. But not all stations have ticket offices and they're not open 24/7, not even at the airports!Why on earth can't they just issue an e-ticket for your devices countless other companies do and they use this archaic and convoluted system only they know. Perhaps they can't be bothered.

Suddenly a tall GWR staff member wearing a black mask with short black hair launched himself at me and shouted “where are you going?” In a tone which suggested I am totally devoid of a brain. He was glaring at me so I took a pause as I couldn’t work out why I was being spoken to in this way and for a moment wasn’t even sure whether he was a member of staff owing to his complete lack of professionalism. He continued, again in a mocking tone, “this train will leave in a minute so you need to know where you’re going”, my partner then confirmed where we were headed to which the GWR member of staff pointed at platform 13 where the 2.39pm service to Great Malvern from BTM (the train we required, 23rd October) was arriving into the platform. “That one” he spat, towards my partner. A much more helpful member of staff almost seemed to intervene at this point as if also dumbstruck by his colleague’s rudeness and confirmed what we had just been told. As we went to board the train I remarked “slightly rude, but thank you” as I was disgusted at the way we had been treated. His anger came out of nowhere and we had not sought any help so his presence was a surprise. We would of been grateful for his assistance had it not been brought forward with abrasiveness and contempt. I was hardly holding up the other train as I was nowhere near it and after all, if confused passengers miss their train, that’s their fault, so there was no need for any of his attitude. The situation was compounded by the fact that as our train left the platform and began on its journey we turned to the passenger window and clocked the same member of staff on the platform waving at the carriage and blowing a kiss! Perhaps this was jokingly intended for the driver of the train but as it came so soon after our minor altercation it seemed too much of a coincidence. The action also seemed to be deliberately sarcastic and however you cut it, it’s rather strange behaviour! He clearly has little time for members of the public and is deeply dissatisfied in his role and he certainly should be nowhere near customers. He seemed to be fizzing with anger and attitude so I can only assume we were not the only recipients of his particular brand of charm this afternoon.  I would add I have never had a problem with train staff before and think they do a marvellous job, often under immense pressure. Coming from a customer service background myself I can appreciate that totally. However, I hope this complaint is taken seriously and the member of staff in question (whom, unfortunately I am not able to name) is given thorough customer service training and guidance on how to maintain his composure and control his anger.

Same on the way back FIRST CLASS only for part of the journey. We really loved sitting on Taunton station for 45 minutes waiting for the train, it was only the Passenger Assist staff who kept us going. Why GWR seeing that you are getting money from the Government are you so uncaring of your customers and the damage you are inflicting on the West Country. Our Hotel had had quite a few regular guests cancel as they were unable to book suitable trains.Thank you for the response nearly a month later however over a month ago I had complained to customer services and given them ALL details - nothing back from them at all after 5 weeks.

While waiting for the train to leave I went to the toilet and could not unlock the door by pressing the usual lock/unlock button. I pressed the emergency button but no one spoke to me through the intercom. After a few minutes of waiting I called my husband (luckily I had my phone on me) who came and prised the door open manually. I would hate to be in a real emergency on GWR. Then there  a message was broadcast that the train would not divide after all. By this time the train was moving so we had to walk the whole length of it with our luggage. The conductor was very apologetic and found us seats together. He said the notice board had put up the wrong message. The return journey passed without incident, to my relief. title: Only Great at Dissapointment
content: Service is regularly late which is disappointing considering the ever rising ticket costs. Prior to Covid, the service update just cased more unecessary chaos for commuters leaving many of us worse off to either raise ticket prices (by removing split ticket destinations from peak times) or removing some smaller local services all together. title: Lost suitcase
content: I forgot my bag on a train from London to Reading and the station management at Reading/Oxford/Paddington were excellent in helping me return it securely. They were compassionate and empathetic to my concerns and tried to reassure me. They went out of their way to call different stations to see if my bag had been found. Once it had been found I was immediately emailed with a photograph and I could go pick it up on that day. Not only were professional in their dealings but they handled the matter with great care and empathy. I am extremely grateful.

title: Great website and awesome service
content: I will be booking tickets for me and my Son to visit Bournemouth in early August. I found the GWR website very user friendly and easy to navigate. It quickly showed the availability and prices for my chosen dates. I was surprised how good the prices are and indeed GWR are far cheaper than any of the various other sites on the internet. I won’t bother with them in the future and will go straight to GWR to book tickets.I did have a query and needed to contact GWR to seek clarification. It clearly shows how you can contact them using Twitter / WattsApp / Phone or e mail. It states you can use WattsApp up to 11pm so at 9.15pm Saturday evening I sent them a message on WattsApp.I thought I would probably get a reply within a couple of days and was amazed that Josh in their customer service team replied within 30 minutes!!His tone was very polite and he answered my question straightaway. This really is awesome service and the best experience I’ve had from any rail operator. Josh deserves some recognition for sure and thanks to GWR for making it all so easy. Kind regards Simon

content: I applied for a refund on 16th March, 64 working days ago and still no refund of my season ticket. I initially contacted them after the standard 28 days they normally take to reply. Then I was told it would be 56 days. I've tried emailing since and all I am given is excuses and told it has been escalated to finance. I'm even more concerned as some have been asked for card details and as I haven't, I'm really no further ahead than when I started this process in March. Having been furloughed and faced salary cuts, this is already an anxious time, which is being exacerbated by GWR.

title: Refund requested 82 days ago and counting
content: Requested refund on season ticket on 27nd March. Still waiting. Kept being told that the processing time had increased, then that it was passed on to the escalation team for payment within 2 weeks which didn't happen. The escalation team was not responding to being chased for over a week after that, then came up with an issue "processing" the payment (whatever the hell that means) which has now been going on for a week. Contacted the complaints department 10 days ago and no sign of life either. Considering that I have been furloughed on reduced pay and that the exorbitant cost of the ticket was covered by a season ticket loan that I still need to reimburse, this keeps getting worse. I'm discussing with my company a WFH schedule going forward so that I don't have to get a season ticket ever again because this experience, in addition to the crowded and delayed trains when they were functioning has been nothing short of appaling.

content: Still waiting for my claim dated 30.3.20.no contact nothing,this is deliberate company policy to keep refund money,im sure this is called fraud.kevin gordon.

title: Don’t book GWR Advance tickets.
content: In April 2020 I bought train tickets to connect with flights from Gatwick Airport. GWR advise me not to travel as my journeys are not essential. That’s understandable. However as I bought Advance tickets I’m told I am not eligible for a refund. GWR Customer Services staff suggest changing my travel dates to a later date. Unfortunately the 12 week window for Advance tickets has disappeared and is only 8 days after my flight, so pretty useless.I’ve paid for journeys I should not take. I can’t get a refund. I can’t book a reasonable alternative service. GWR have taken my payment and offer no reasonable travel options. Terrible company.

title: Disappointing
content: I've now been waiting 74 days for my season ticket refund, and I'm disappointed.  If the GWR Twitter page is anything to go by, I know I'm not the only person that has been waiting a significant period for their refund to be processed. I'm aware that the Refunds Team has received an unprecedented number of requests, but to keep customers waiting for their money for so long, and at such a challenging time, is quite distressing.  People have lost their jobs and have been furloughed - this money could be the difference in someone making their rent payment or buying food.  The lack of compassion and empathy for customers is both astounding and disappointing. Also, I imagine many people with season tickets don't just have £4k+ lying around - they use loan schemes through work to pay for their travel. What if people have been made redundant without paying off their season ticket loan?  Please, please, please have a conscience and give people their money back within a reasonable timeframe.   (The two stars are for the GWR Customer Service team - you've always been helpful.  Your responsiveness and customer care are much appreciated; it makes the silence from the rest of GWR on this matter all the more glaring.)

title: GWR fails to refund after 67 days
content: I applied for two refunds from GWR on on 24 March. It’s now 67 days later  there’s been NO refund. GWR have failed to proactively contact me and when contacting them (several times) they’ve given conflicting and woolly responses. Their sole accurate message being that they’re received the claims but they’ve been too busy to refund within the usual timeframe. They say they have had to double it. It’s now nearly two weeks beyond the extended timeframe so that was wrong information . GWR need to understand that their customers have also been impacted by the crisis as well as them. Busy GWR will be. And no doubt fewer staff. Everyone can understand that brings challenges. However the extreme delay now begins to feel like poorly managed procedures at the least,  a reluctance to respect their customers and a seemingly  unwillingness to refund. With such overwhelmingly poor feedback GWR need to improve performance fast.

title: I have no choice but to use this…
content: I have no choice but to use this dreadful and rip off train operator.  I would be embarressed to look at the reviews here if I was the MD, wake up GWR !!.  Every train I seem to use either gets cancelled or delayed that I miss my connection at Temple Meads. Forget the Delay / Repay mine got refused despite them cancelling the train !! A cancelled train is a breach of the ticket I brought, not a delay because I got the next train !!  they cancelled the service I was booked on so that's a full refund, just like buying anything when the goods/services aren't fulfilled. Boycott them if you can, they deserve all they get and their demise will only be themselves to blame. Nationalisation can't come sooner to GWR. I await a copy and pasted reply from Bradley. title: Why is the company still running?
content: Why is the company still running? One of the very worst train operators in the UK. Now becoming increasingly standard practice to run three standard class carriages London-Swansea: 4 of these of my 6 trips in recent months. Often no apology or explanation, with dozens standing. After months of disruption and claims about improved new trains and more seats, habitually running disgracefully short trains, with vastly less seats, and the seats themselves on new trains infamous for being probably the most uncomfortable in UK. A recent journey with 3 broken toilets, no water in basins, and severe overcrowding would be a tremendous way to help spread the coronavirus efficiently. GWR is almost certainly running these absurdly short trains to avoid outright cancellations, for which it would be financially penalised. The greatest advert for Renationalisation you could possibly imagine. No one would use this company if they had a choice.
